designs.name: MiniFly Minimal Fail-Closed Gates (MFG-1): four choke points, one stdlib checker, three skills
designs.thesis:
The eight costliest MiniFly incidents were silent failures that produced wrong evidence. Each one could have been detected in seconds from an artifact that already existed, or could have existed cheaply, before the expensive stage:
- Package B: one technical receipt per arm. N_old_rel performed all 288 relation writes while the spec said 0, and its state digest equalled W's.
- v4: the sign of one directional fixture.
- V6-R1: the cue/noise SNR from the init formulas (0.00268 vs 0.1), already written in LEARNING_RULE.md.
- STOP-ONLY: a fixed-length-1 truncation of the arm's own saved stream.
- v5.1: a port fixture run at production density (0.0354, not 0.02) that had to fail.
- LEARNED-BANK: a BP/FROZEN table on the split. A fail-open reducer was also visible on 3 synthetic rows.
- Post-outcome amendments: a hash diff of the endpoint block.
- Claim inflation: a closed enum plus a generated headline.

MFG-1 does not try to encode good research practice. It puts four fail-closed choke points where compute or credibility is spent:
- **LOCK**: before the first scored value on any world.
- **ROSTER**: before spending beyond a small technical allowance.
- **OFFICIAL**: before a confirmation, adoption or pointer-grade claim.
- **PUBLISH/POINTER**: before anything other agents read first.

One Python-stdlib checker (tools/minifly_check) backs these points. It owns, for the whole program, the canonical exact-own-EOS scorer and the shortcut ladder. A delivery writes only its decision rule (verdict.py: decide(rows, lock)). That removes the shared-semantics auditor problem, because no per-delivery code computes the metric that the gate judges.

Three rules hold throughout:
- A missing artifact, a null input or a check that cannot run counts as FAIL.
- CANNOT_TEST_CLAIM_AS_SPECIFIED is an unpenalized honest exit. Literature: an abort option sharply reduced cheating.
- The tier is computed, not declared down. Official, confirmation, adoption and pointer updates are always tier 2.

The checker itself is tested three ways:
- A regression corpus that rebuilds each historical incident synthetically, plus clean fixtures that must pass.
- Reviewer-seeded canary mutations of each delivery's own artifacts, which the executor cannot anticipate.
- Recall on held-out incidents it was never built from.

Only an owner-recorded decision with monotone strictness can change the checker.

Generalization is measured with numbers rather than told as a story:
- **Learner level**: G = held non-trivial exact own-EOS minus max(best shortcut, no-prior-teaching control, chance). It is also reported per taught presentation and at the locked compute snapshot.
- **Research level**: predictions that cite findings are scored against a base-rate forecaster (about 0/8 native E3 successes). The checker's held-out incident recall is the skill-level analogue of E3.

**Deliberately left out until an incident shows they would have caught a silent failure:**
- Environment and import lint. These failures are loud and cost a cycle, never a wrong conclusion.
- An attempt and compute wrapper ledger.
- Typed per-cycle plans and revision taxonomies. These were the source of the padding.
- HMAC commit-reveal seeds and a reserved E3 family. Nothing has yet reached dev E3.
- Operating-characteristic simulation. Only a reachability fixture is mandatory.
- Lineage AST/equation diffs.
- Generated catalogs and a full unit-fact register.
- Prose citation lint.
- A learner-side input tap.
- Decoy tripwires.
- Per-cycle cross-agent sign-off.

skills.name: minifly-stage-gates
skills.description_frontmatter: Use before any MiniFly action that creates or spends evidence: freezing a design, running cycle 0 or any technical/dev cycle that yields a scored value, launching a roster, pilot, official or confirmation run, changing a task, metric, pool, comparator, margin, threshold or guard after any outcome exists, or editing verdict/gate code. Applies to Codex and Claude alike, for every delivery dir <name>_{design|dev}_vN_YYYYMMDD created after the schema-v1 freeze. Says which artifacts each stage needs (ENDPOINT_LOCK.json, ADMISSION.json, receipts, OUTPUTS.jsonl, verdict.py, AMENDMENTS.jsonl, AUTHORIZATION.json), how the stake tier is computed, the one command per stage (python3 -I tools/minifly_check/minifly_check.py gate --stage lock|roster|official <dir>), and what to do on FAIL. Not needed for read-only analysis that changes no claim, pointer or plan.
skills.when_invoked: At design freeze (gate --stage lock). Before writing learner code (cycle-0 testbed screen). After one technical record per arm (gate --stage roster), before any roster, pilot or official run. Before the official run (gate --stage official, with a --dry rehearsal in the last test cycle). Whenever an endpoint field or a lock-covered file would change after any outcome exists. Runners call gate themselves and refuse to start on a nonzero exit (LOCK-13).
key_rules: Lock before look: ENDPOINT_LOCK.json, verdict.py and the hashes of the static import closure (runner, native and verdict entrypoints, resolving literal sys.path.insert paths) are committed before the first scored value on any world, dev included. Tier 2 also requires the lock commit to be on a remote branch, or a reviewer's pre-launch attestation of the lock sha if the owner withholds push.

Cycle 0 before learner code: run the testbed screen on the exact split and input code. An evaluator-side ceiling learner (exact gradient or oracle features) must pass the primary gate. Frozen random features must fail it. If either condition fails, the verdict is CANNOT_TEST_CLAIM_AS_SPECIFIED: redesign, do not implement or tune.

Missing = FAIL. An absent artifact, an unknown schema, a null or NaN gate input, or a check that cannot run blocks the stage. Never skip, stub or hand-write a measurement. ADMISSION.json and OUTPUTS.jsonl are produced only by locked code.

Deliveries write the decision rule, not the metric. verdict.py exposes decide(rows, lock), uses the stdlib only, imports nothing from native or runner files, and assigns no literal True, False or 0 to integrity keys. The checker's canonical scorer computes exact own-EOS from OUTPUTS.jsonl, feeds the rows to decide(), and writes VERDICT.json.

Shortcut ladder before official: dev OUTPUTS.jsonl, including the pre-stop stream_hex, go through score --role dev.
- The ladder contains constant, length-frequency, suffix-k, exact-key, canonical-key, copy-operand, fixed-length-k of the arm's own stream, and mode-repeat.
- The locked rule must FAIL when the candidate is replaced by the best shortcut.
- Every declared comparator must be at least as strong as the best shortcut, or be replaced by it.
- Gains confined to trivial strata (zero operand, identity) do not count.

E3 cadence: if KB/DELIVERY_LEDGER shows two or more consecutive deliveries that did not open a held-E3 endpoint, the next lock must open one (objective_distance.opens_held_E3 = true) or cite an owner waiver.

Never edit tools/minifly_check, .claude/skills/minifly-*, AGENTS.md, KB/CONSTRAINTS.json or KB/USER_DECISIONS.jsonl in a commit range that also touches a delivery. Never edit a lock-covered file after the lock without an amendment. Never rerun a failed or inconvenient official run.

Honest exits are first-class and carry no penalty: CANNOT_TEST_CLAIM_AS_SPECIFIED, NO_ADVANCE, and INVALID with reason TREATMENT_NOT_DELIVERED. Meta-progress counts only sealed-world G, never gates passed or cycles completed.

Cycles are free-form and end on a decision (continue, revise, stop or escalate), not on a count. designs_tried_k is computed as the number of distinct native_closure_sha values in dev outputs, and the headline prints 'best of k'.

The tier is computed as the maximum of the declared tier and the tier derived from budget and stage. Tier 0: no scored candidate endpoint and 1 CPU-h or less. Tier 1: dev/technical, 10 CPU-h or less and 50k records or fewer; these thresholds come from CONSTRAINTS. Tier 2: anything bigger, plus every official, confirmation, adoption or pointer update.

skills.name: minifly-claims-publish
skills.description_frontmatter: Use whenever you write or change anything another agent or Mr. Zhou will read as a MiniFly result or status: REPORT.md, STATUS/SUMMARY/VERDICT JSON, CLAIM.json, PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/CURRENT_*.json pointers, catalog or memo rows, KB/FINDINGS.jsonl, or a next-step memo that quotes earlier numbers; also when a later analysis narrows an earlier finding and when scoring a design's registered predictions. Enforces the closed claim vocabulary (E0-E4/NONE; PASS, FAIL, INVALID, INCOMPLETE, NOT_OPENED, CANNOT_TEST_CLAIM_AS_SPECIFIED), a tool-generated headline carrying the objective metric and best shortcut, 'confirm' only on sealed fresh worlds, append-only findings with narrowing links, and pointers generated from CLAIM.json. Command: python3 -I tools/minifly_check/minifly_check.py gate --stage publish <dir> (add --stage pointer --pointer <file> for CURRENT_* edits).
skills.when_invoked: At the end of any delivery, any tier. Before editing any CURRENT_* pointer, catalog or memo row. When a reanalysis narrows a prior result (for example the STOP-ONLY +22.10pp versus FIXED_1). When a next-design memo cites earlier numbers. When scoring the predictions registered in ENDPOINT_LOCK.json.
key_rules: Generate the verdict, do not write it. minifly_check.py claim <dir> builds CLAIM.json and the headline from three inputs: VERDICT.json (the locked verdict.py applied to canonical rows), SCORES.json and the lock. The first non-empty line of REPORT.md must equal the generated headline, for example: 'FAIL | earned E1 (attempted E3) | held exact own-EOS 0.0% vs best shortcut copy_operand 3.1% | OLD final 0.3% | G -3.1pp | 8 DEV worlds | best of k=2'.

The objective metric goes beside every result: final held and OLD/NEW exact own-EOS (or 'not_measured'), best shortcut name and value, headroom, G, worlds n and role, and best-of-k. It appears in the headline, in CLAIM.json and in every pointer. A component PASS without these fields is rejected.
The token confirm* may appear only when worlds_role = SEALED_CONFIRM and the world-freshness check WLD-01 passed. Results on fewer than min_worlds worlds are PILOT.
No soft verdict words in any sentence that names a gate, guard or the primary: largely, mostly, in part, partial, partially, nearly, promising, essentially, approved, met in part.

Findings are append-only rows in KB/FINDINGS.jsonl, one to three per delivery, each with conditions and the best shortcut. To narrow or retract a finding, append a row with narrowed_by or supersedes. Any pointer or catalog row that quotes a narrowed finding must cite the narrowing row.
Score every registered prediction (hit/miss, interval score, Brier for p_pass) and never delete one. Append transfer_ok or transfer_failed to each cited finding.

CURRENT_*.json files are rewritten only as minifly.pointer.v1 copies of CLAIM.json fields (claim_sha256). The previous pointer is snapshotted into *_POINTER_HISTORY first. No bare pass/confirm/success booleans and no absolute local paths. Existing adopted pointers are never touched except by an owner-authorized update.
Posthoc analyses are welcome. They are labelled POSTHOC and never feed VERDICT.json.
A tier-2 claim needs the published verification subset: OUTPUTS.jsonl (or a hash-verified compressed copy), manifests, the lock, receipt digests and the GATE reports. Without them it is rejected.
artifacts_produced: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/CURRENT_<track>.json in minifly.pointer.v1 plus snapshot in *_POINTER_HISTORY

skills.name: minifly-independent-audit
skills.description_frontmatter: Use when you review a MiniFly delivery you did not author (required once per tier-2 delivery, after ADMISSION.json exists and before any roster, official or confirmation run, adoption or pointer update); when you find or suspect a defect, shortcut, reward-hacking route or recurring failure in any delivery, old or new; and whenever anyone proposes changing .claude/skills/minifly-*, tools/minifly_check (checks, thresholds, corpus, EXPECTED.json), AGENTS.md, PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/KB/CONSTRAINTS.json or USER_DECISIONS.jsonl. Covers the executing review and cheapest-shortcut attempt, the seeded canary run, REVIEW.json, filing incidents that close only with a new check plus corpus fixture, and the governance rules that stop gates and skills being edited to pass (owner decision, monotone strictness, separation from delivery branches, held-out incident recall).
skills.when_invoked: One review event per tier-2 delivery, by the other agent family. Whenever any agent finds a defect, shortcut or suspicious pass, in a current or historical delivery (historical findings are recorded through retro annotations only). Whenever a change to a protected path is proposed. Whenever a new incident source arrives, such as the pre-Full151 archive analysis.
key_rules: Reviewer differs from author. A tier-2 review is valid only from the other agent family, as shown by the Acting-Agent commit trailer and the REVIEW.json identity fields. Codex commits as 'Pencilbard', so git author is never used. There is one review event per tier-2 delivery, after ADMISSION exists and before any roster or official run.

Execute, do not just read. A review needs at least one executed check with committed repo-relative script and output hashes and a CPU cap. Acceptable checks: rerun admit.py on a technical world; feed a gate an input it must reject; run the next stage unchanged on an oracle upstream; trace a headline or admission number to its producing line and coefficients. Read-only findings are UNVERIFIED and can neither block nor clear.

Try to cheat. Attempt the cheapest policy that passes the locked rule (a shortcut, degenerate output, trivial strata or a structured SHUF) and record the attempt with its script. If it succeeds, it blocks the delivery.

Seeded canary: run canary <dir> --seed <fresh hex you choose after reading the lock> --n 20. Every mutant must be caught, and the unmutated copy must pass. A surviving mutant is a checker gap: file an incident.

Reconcile every finding with the status enum: CONFIRMED, CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION, REFUTED, NEW_DEFECT or SCOPE_LIMITED. The author reconciles before launch, and no blocking finding may be open at launch.

Incidents close only with a check. Append every defect to KB/INCIDENTS.jsonl, recording whether the current checker caught it (caught_at_discovery, checker_sha). It closes only when a check id and a synthetic corpus fixture with an EXPECTED.json entry exist.

Held-out recall: new incident sources are scored against the frozen checker before any check is written for them, and selftest --heldout reports recall per checker version. Raising corpus recall without raising held-out recall counts as overfitting.
Do not optimize agents, prompts or skills against flag counts. The kit's own score is three things only: checker held-out recall, prediction calibration, and sealed-world G.

Lessons from the delivering agent are inputs, not truth. The reviewer lists what the author's notes omit. Example: LEARNED-BANK's notes omit the fail-open summarize.py, the lock closure gaps and the task's distance from E3.

tools.purpose: Single CLI dispatcher and the gate bundles. It chooses checks by stage and computed tier, writes checks/GATE_<stage>_<utc>.json and returns exit codes that launchers obey. It also runs a cached selftest first whenever its own sha differs from the last recorded selftest.
tools.cli:
python3 -I tools/minifly_check/minifly_check.py gate --stage {lock|roster|official|publish|pointer} <delivery_dir> [--pointer PATH] [--dry] [--json]
Other subcommands: score, claim, canary, selftest, governance, retro, kb-score.
Exit codes: 0 = PASS; 1 = FAIL; 2 = MISSING_OR_INVALID_INPUT, treated as FAIL; 3 = CHECKER_ERROR, treated as FAIL.
checks: TIER-01: tier = max(declared, computed from lock.budget and stage). Official, confirmation, adoption and pointer stages are always tier 2.
SELF-01: checker_sha256 (all files under tools/minifly_check) equals the blob at git HEAD, so no locally modified checker is in use. The corpus selftest has passed for this sha.
SCHEMA-01: refuses legacy (non-v1) deliveries with exit 2 and the hint 'use retro'. It never writes into legacy directories.
Bundles: lock = LOCK-*, AMD-*. roster = LOCK-*, AMD-*, ADM-*, RED-01..09. official = roster + LAD-*, RED-10, REV-01, AUT-01, WLD-01 when SEALED_CONFIRM. publish = AMD-*, CLM-*. pointer = PTR-*.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Any exception, unknown schema version, missing file, null or NaN in a gate-relevant field, or failed git call produces FAIL with the reason. There is no --force and no --skip flag. NOT_APPLICABLE exists only in retro mode. The report always records checker_sha256, git HEAD, lock_sha256 and the UTC time.
tools.self_tests: selftest runs every bundle over tools/minifly_check/corpus/* and compares the fired check ids with EXPECTED.json. Incident fixtures must fire a superset of their expected ids, and clean fixtures C00a/C00b must fire none. Target runtime is under 15 s.

tools.purpose: Lock, timing, closure, purity, isolation and amendment checks. These are static and git-only and never import delivery code.
tools.cli: Invoked by gate --stage lock|roster|official|publish. Standalone: python3 -I tools/minifly_check/minifly_check.py gate --stage lock <dir>
checks: LOCK-01: ENDPOINT_LOCK.json exists with schema minifly.endpoint_lock.v1 and every required field is non-null.

LOCK-02: the contract block is complete. claim_level_target is an enum value; causal_control_arm and positive_control_arm exist in arms[]; recitation_countermodels is non-empty; the exposure_manifest and exposure_streams files exist.

LOCK-03: primary.metric is exact_own_eos or balanced_exact_own_eos, with unconditional = true. Otherwise gate_type is forced to component and CLAIM may not use gate_type objective. This is the STOP-ONLY conditional primary.

LOCK-04: margin_abs, absolute_floor above chance, a non-empty comparators list and min_worlds of at least 8 unless worlds_role is PILOT. Every threshold is at or above its CONSTRAINTS.threshold_floors value.

LOCK-05: verdict.py and every file in the static AST import closure of files.runner, files.native and files.verdict are in closure_sha256 with matching hashes. The closure resolves literal sys.path.insert paths. This catches the V6 audit_results.py outside SOURCE_LOCK and LEARNED-BANK's partial lock.

LOCK-06: the commit that introduced the current lock sha precedes the first commit adding results/**, receipts or OUTPUTS*. At tier 2, the lock commit must also be contained in a remote-tracking branch (git branch -r --contains), or REVIEW.json must carry a pre-launch lock attestation.

LOCK-07: native purity. The import closure of files.native contains none of CONSTRAINTS.native_forbidden_patterns (autograd, .backward(, requires_grad, attention modules, transformers, ELM). Native files import no files.evaluator file. Evaluator-only BP ceiling learners remain allowed.

LOCK-08-ISO: verdict.py uses stdlib imports from the allowlist only (math, statistics, json, itertools, collections, fractions) and imports nothing from native or runner files. This addresses the common-mode auditor of FM-01.

LOCK-08-LIT: no literal True, False or 0 is assigned to keys or variables matching the integrity regex (_ok, _passed, overlap, _verified, no_*, all_*) in verdict, audit or report files. This is the V6 audit_results.py:97 pattern.

LOCK-09: E3 cadence. deliveries_since_last_opened_E3 is computed from KB/DELIVERY_LEDGER.jsonl. If it is 2 or more and objective_distance.opens_held_E3 is false, e3_cadence.waiver_user_decision must resolve in USER_DECISIONS.

LOCK-10: constraints_sha256 equals the sha256 of KB/CONSTRAINTS.json at lock time. Fields that CONSTRAINTS governs (warmup ceiling, raw bytes, own EOS) equal the constraint values or cite a USER_DECISIONS id.

LOCK-11: predictions[] has at least one primary prediction (point and interval, or p_pass) plus one per admission measurement. Each cites basis_findings that exist in FINDINGS.jsonl (or 'none') and includes base_rate_forecast.

LOCK-12: admission_thresholds.analytic_input_snr is either a number at or above analytic_input_snr_min, or 'not_derivable'; in the latter case ADM-INPUT becomes mandatory at tier 1. V6-R1 fails at design time on 0.00268/0.1 = 0.027.
LOCK-13: runner or launch script invokes 'minifly_check.py gate --stage roster|official' and aborts on a nonzero exit (AST or grep).
AMD-01: there is a hash chain from the first committed lock sha to the current sha, each link an AMENDMENTS.jsonl row with old and new sha. An unexplained lock diff is FAIL.
AMD-03: reason is one of ceiling, testbed_invalid, measurement_defect or operational. testbed_invalid requires an ADMISSION testbed table on the original endpoint showing ceiling FAIL or floor PASS.
AMD-04: no official world id appears in any outcome artifact committed before the latest amendment.

AMD-05: any lock-covered file changed after the lock commit (git diff) without an amendment row is FAIL. A change to verdict.py after the lock additionally requires a tier-2 reviewer sign-off or a USER_DECISIONS id. This addresses tests edited after they failed (FM-15).
tools.fail_closed_behavior: If git history is unavailable, LOCK-06 and AMD-01/02/04/05 are FAIL, never skipped. An unresolvable import counts as an omitted closure file and is FAIL. A missing CONSTRAINTS.json or USER_DECISIONS.jsonl is FAIL.
tools.self_tests: Corpus fixtures: C09 (LEARNED-BANK post-outcome T-MOD to T-PAR amendment), C13 (V6 verdict outside lock plus literals), C14 (Package B common-mode auditor importing branch_allows), C17 (lock and results in one commit), C05 (V6 analytic SNR). Clean fixture C00a must pass. The git layer accepts a fixture timeline.json in place of real git for corpus runs.

tools.purpose: Behavioral admission before spend. It validates ADMISSION.json and raw technical receipts against the spec-side declarations in ENDPOINT_LOCK. Expectations come from SPEC declarations (arms[].zero_channels and production_params), never from executor helpers.
tools.cli: Invoked by gate --stage roster|official <dir>
checks: ADM-01: ADMISSION.json has schema minifly.admission.v1, lock_sha256 equal to the current lock, a producer script inside the closure with matching sha, worlds drawn only from lock.worlds.technical, and a commit before the first roster output.

ADM-TB-CEIL / ADM-TB-FLOOR: the ceiling learner passes the primary gate, the floor learner fails it, and split_sha256 equals the lock. A failure sets the outcome CANNOT_TEST_CLAIM_AS_SPECIFIED. This catches LEARNED-BANK T-MOD (BP held 0.00/0.11) and CARRY/CMP (FROZEN 0.73-0.89).

ADM-CTRL-ZERO / ADM-CTRL-DIGEST / ADM-CTRL-DOSE: these read receipts/<world>/<arm>.json directly. For each arm with zero_channels, its writes on those channels are 0, W's writes on them are above 0, state_digest differs from W's, and realized_dose is at least min_realized_dose. This catches Package B (288 writes, identical digests) and CREDIT (0.3% attenuation). A failure sets the outcome INVALID with reason TREATMENT_NOT_DELIVERED.

ADM-DIR: for every port and each declared sign, target_margin_delta_vs_passive is above 0, zero_coef_digest_equals_passive is true and zero_replay_applications equals 0. This catches the v4 negated residual and the [-0:] replay slice.

ADM-FIX: every key shared between a fixture's params and lock.production_params is equal within the declared tolerance, and production keys missing from a fixture are FAIL. This catches the v5.1 density of 0.02 against 0.0354 and calibration without REPLY frame types.

ADM-GATE-NEG / ADM-GATE-POS: every gate with used_in_verdict, and the primary, has at least one negative fixture with result false and at least one positive or oracle fixture with result true. A gate without a demonstrated FAIL may not be used in the verdict. This catches the v5.1 port that 'can't fail'.

ADM-INPUT: input_contrast.ratio is at least input_contrast_min (different-input distance over same-input different-noise distance), and prompt_id_loo_acc is at least chance plus prompt_id_margin_min. This catches V6-R1 (Jaccard 0.014 vs 0.98) and v5.1 aliasing of 12 types onto 8.
ADM-ACQ: taught_acquisition.candidate_exact is at least best_countermodel_exact plus taught_acq_margin_min on the short prefix. This catches NATIVE-BIND V2.1 and V6-R1 taught rates of 0-8%.
ADM-SHUF: shuf_truth_agreement lies within the band, default [0.35, 0.65]. This catches the derangement that taught anti-parity.

ADM-EXPO: held items, canonicalized (operands sorted for a+b, whitespace and leading zeros normalized), have an empty intersection with the canonicalized items of every feedback_bearing stream in lock.exposure_streams.
ADM-BUDGET: lock.budget is within the AUTHORIZATION caps at tier 2, and lock.schedule.paired_atomic is true, meaning W and all its controls are scheduled per world together.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: A missing receipt for any declared arm, a missing fixture for any declared port or sign, or a missing field is FAIL. Receipts take precedence over ADMISSION summaries when both exist, and any disagreement between them is FAIL.
tools.self_tests: Corpus: C01 Package B identical controls, C02 CREDIT inert dose, C03 v4 reversed sign, C04 v5.1 port fixture at 0.02 with no negative fixture, C05 V6 cue/noise, C06 T-MOD untestable, C07 CARRY separable, C08 SHUF derangement. Clean C00a must pass. Canary operators M01-M04 and M07 target this module.

tools.purpose: The canonical program-wide scorer and shortcut ladder. It reads saved outputs only and never runs a learner. This is the one place where exact own-EOS, balanced accuracy, strata, G and the countermodels are computed for every delivery, so no delivery-specific auditor can share semantics with its executor.
tools.cli:
python3 -I tools/minifly_check/minifly_check.py score <delivery_dir> --role {dev|official} [--json]
Writes results/<role>/SCORES.json. For the official role it also calls the locked verdict.decide(rows, lock) in a subprocess (python3 -I, delivery dir only on the path, 20 s timeout) and writes VERDICT.json.
checks: LAD-01: OUTPUTS.jsonl rows exist for every (world, arm, pool, checkpoint) the lock declares, and the counts equal lock.primary.n_items_per_pool. Denominators come from the lock, never from the data.
Canonical metric: an item is exact when own_eos is true, emitted_hex equals expected_hex and answer_path is native. A balanced variant groups by expected answer.

LAD-02: substitution test. Replace the candidate's rows with the best shortcut's rows and call decide(). If the verdict is PASS, the result is FAIL 'gate non-discriminating vs <shortcut>'. This catches STOP-ONLY's FIXED_1, at about 0.19-0.21 conditional stopping against DIRECT 0.

LAD-03: every declared comparator scores at least the best shortcut on dev data. Otherwise the result is FAIL WEAK_COMPARATOR, fixed by adding the shortcut to the comparators through an amendment. This catches DIRECT at 0 in 86/96 checkpoints and LEARNED-BANK's below-chance FROZEN and SHUF.

LAD-04: the primary excludes or separately reports lock.trivial_strata_excluded (zero_operand, identity, copy-solvable). The candidate's headroom on required strata must be positive, not only on trivial ones. This catches the V6 x+0 route.
LAD-05: every primary-counted item has answer_path native. modal_fraction and output entropy are reported for every pool, with a WARN above 0.9 modal fraction (the V6 byte 0x31).
RED-10: two-source agreement. When the delivery also saved its own primary numbers, they equal the canonical scorer's within 1e-9.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Missing stream_hex makes the CM-FIXED family impossible to compute, which is FAIL at tier 2 and WARN at tier 1. A row-count mismatch against the lock, or any decide() exception, timeout or non-enum output, is FAIL. Non-addition prompts skip only the operand-based countermodels, and the skip is recorded.
tools.self_tests: Corpus: C11 STOP-ONLY (rows where FIXED_1 scores 10.645% against candidate 11.263%, with a DIRECT comparator at 0), C12 V6 zero-operand route, and clean C00a with hand-computed expected SCORES.json values to the 4th decimal. Canary operators M05 (candidate replaced by its FIXED_k stream) and M06 (comparator rows dropped) target this module. Runtime is about 10 s per 1e6 rows.

tools.purpose: Tests the delivery's decision rule (verdict.decide) on synthetic fixtures. This tests the test, so that fail-open reducers and unreachable gates are found before data exists.
tools.cli: Invoked by gate --stage roster|official <dir>. Standalone: python3 -I tools/minifly_check/minifly_check.py gate --stage roster <dir> (the RED checks only run when ENDPOINT_LOCK and verdict.py exist).
checks:
The rule is run on synthetic canonical rows generated from the lock's arms, worlds, pools and strata:
- RED-01: clean positive (candidate 0.9 on required strata, controls and shortcuts at chance, all worlds) must PASS. Otherwise the gate is unreachable (FM-05, persistent_core ratio gate).
- RED-02: candidate equal to the strongest control must not PASS.
- RED-03: one comparator or gate arm missing must give INVALID or INCOMPLETE (LEARNED-BANK missing COPY or ORACLE).
- RED-04: fewer worlds than lock.min_worlds must not PASS (LEARNED-BANK 1/1 'supported').
- RED-05: a gate input of None or NaN must not PASS ('is not False' fail-open).
- RED-06: all worlds with world_role dev must give DEV_NOT_EVIDENCE (rehearsal on D3).
- RED-07: candidate exactly 1e-9 below comparator plus margin must not PASS.
- RED-08: gain only on trivial strata must not PASS.
- RED-09: primary passes but the OLD guard fails must not PASS.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Any fixture violation, exception, timeout or non-enum verdict is FAIL. verdict.py that fails LOCK-08-ISO (non-stdlib import) is never imported, and the result is FAIL.

GOV-SKILL: each .claude/skills/minifly-*/SKILL.md has valid YAML frontmatter (name, description of 1024 chars or fewer) and a body under 400 lines. AGENTS.md still points to the three skills.

designs.roles_and_independence:
**Four roles, with independence placed only where it buys the most per minute.**

**(1) Executor.** Usually Codex, but any agent can hold this role.
- Writes ENDPOINT_LOCK.json, the learner, the runner, admit.py and verdict.py.
- Runs the gates, and is trusted to that extent at tier 1.
- Must not touch protected paths in any commit range that also touches a delivery.
- Must not hand-write measurements. ADMISSION, receipts and OUTPUTS come only from locked code.

**(2) Canonical scorer: the checker itself.**
- Program-wide, written once, and tested by the corpus.
- Owns the metric, the shortcut ladder, G and the substitution test.
- This replaces per-delivery 'independent' auditors that imported or transcribed executor code (Package B branch_allows, STOP-ONLY audit.py, V6 manifest rebuild). Independence is structural: a delivery contributes only the decision rule, and that rule is tested on synthetic fixtures before data exists.

**(3) Reviewer: the other agent family.** Claude reviews Codex deliveries and vice versa.
- Required at tier 2 only, as one review event after ADMISSION exists and before any roster or official spend. That point covers the design and the first technical evidence while nothing expensive has run. UF-28: pre-implementation reviews prevented runs; post-publication reviews only reinterpreted them.
- Must execute at least one check, pick the canary seed, and attempt the cheapest passing shortcut.
- Identity comes from the Acting-Agent commit trailer and the REVIEW.json fields, never from the git author. Codex commits as 'Pencilbard', the owner's identity.

**(4) Owner (Mr. Zhou).**
- Sole authority for CONSTRAINTS, threshold floors, tier thresholds and USER_DECISIONS.
- Agents transcribe his words verbatim; he spot-checks.
- Every one of these needs his explicit recorded decision: scope or objective-distance increase, endpoint amendment after outcomes, E3-cadence waiver, adoption, any checker or skill change, and any loosening.

**Stated independence limits.**
- Tier 1 has no independent reviewer. This is accepted because tier-1 outputs are stamped DEV, may not use confirm*, and cannot reach pointers without passing tier 2.
- The checker is a new common mode: one scorer bug affects every delivery. This is mitigated by clean fixtures with hand-computed values and by the reviewer's trace-a-number check.
- USER_DECISIONS records are agent-transcribed, so a fabricated decision is possible. The mitigations are the append-only check, mandatory session references and owner spot-checks. No in-repo mechanism can authenticate the owner while Codex commits under his name.
designs.rsi_mechanism:
**Three improvement loops, each with a numeric target, plus explicit guards against meta-Goodhart (agents improving the score of the loop rather than the loop).**

**(1) Incident -> check loop: improves the checker.**
- Any agent who finds a defect appends a row to KB/INCIDENTS.jsonl. The row records whether the current frozen checker caught it (caught_at_discovery, checker_sha).
- If the checker missed it, the fix is a new or strengthened check, a synthetic corpus fixture that reproduces the incident (the C-series shows the pattern) and an EXPECTED.json entry.
- The fix merges only through governance: a 'User-Decision' trailer, a commit range separate from any delivery, a passing selftest, and monotone strictness.
- An incident closes only when its fixture exists. This turns 'lessons stay prose' (FM-26) into a mechanical invariant.

**(2) Held-out generalization of the checker: the skill-level analogue of E3.**
- Incidents from sources not used to build the current version are scored against the frozen checker before anyone writes a check for them. Sources are the pre-Full151 archive analysis, now in progress, and every future incident at discovery.
- selftest --heldout reports held-out recall per checker version.
- A version that raises corpus recall but not held-out recall is overfitting the eight incidents. Held-out recall, not corpus pass rate, is the checker's score.

**(3) Prediction loop: improves the knowledge base and the designers.**
- Each lock registers numeric predictions that cite FINDINGS ids and a base-rate forecast.
- The publish stage scores them: hit or miss, interval score, Brier.
- kb-score reports KB skill against the base-rate forecaster (UF-27, about 0/8 native E3), plus per-finding transfer rates and per-agent calibration.
- Findings whose transfers repeatedly fail get an appended narrowed row.

**Meta-Goodhart guards:**
- Protected paths (skills, checker, corpus, EXPECTED, AGENTS.md, CONSTRAINTS, USER_DECISIONS).
- An owner decision for every protected change. Loosening requires the owner's verbatim words.
- Separation: a delivery and a checker change can never share a commit range.
- Every GATE report records checker_sha256, and publish verifies it equals the committed checker, so a locally patched checker cannot produce a valid pass.
- Reviewer-seeded canaries that the executor cannot anticipate.
- The kit's own progress is measured only by sealed-world G, held-out recall and prediction calibration, never by gates passed, cycles completed or flags avoided. The literature reports that optimizing against monitors produces obfuscation.

**Anti-ratchet.** Once a quarter, or every 5 v1 deliveries, the owner reviews checks with zero confirmed catches and their measured runtime and minutes (from CLAIM.ceremony_minutes and the GATE reports). Pruning a check is a loosening and goes through governance. This keeps the minimal kit from growing back into the padded rituals the history shows.

**Skills improve the same way.** A SKILL.md edit is a protected change. It is validated by the selftest and by re-running gates on the last N v1 deliveries, to confirm that nothing previously caught now passes.
designs.knowledge_mechanism:
The kit keeps the smallest knowledge structure that makes generalization from unit knowledge measurable at two levels.

**Learner level: units to held-out composition.**
- Every schema-v1 delivery with byte-addition items reports G, whatever its declared level. G = mean over worlds of [final exact own-EOS of W on held items in required non-trivial strata, minus max(the same for the no-prior-teaching causal control, the best shortcut on the ladder, chance)].
- Companions: G_per_sample (G per taught presentation, from receipts), G at the locked compute snapshot, and OLD_drop (own OLD_END minus own FINAL, never measured against a never-taught arm). These cover the objective's 'per sample and per actual compute' and 'protecting OLD'.
- G resists gaming for four reasons:
  - the shortcut max is computed by the checker from the item set, not by the delivery;
  - trivial strata (zero operand, identity) are excluded;
  - held items are canonicalized and checked against every feedback-bearing stream;
  - only sealed-world G counts as program progress.
- The DELIVERY_LEDGER keeps the G series and deliveries_since_last_opened_E3. This is the mechanical counter to the prerequisite treadmill, in which six of seven deliveries on 10-22/23 were E0/E1 components.

**Research level: unit facts and failure classes to scored predictions.**
- KB/FINDINGS.jsonl is append-only. It is seeded from UF-01..UF-29 with their statuses: UF-15 STOP-ONLY narrowed by FIXED_1; UF-16 CREDIT is an inert manipulation, not a failed recipe; UF-02 V9.9A/B is UNVERIFIABLE_IN_REPO.
- Each row carries conditions (substrate, input code, supplied priors, feedback, dose, comparator and the best shortcut), effect with CI, source path:line, and status with narrowed_by and supersedes links.
- A design cites the findings its predictions rest on. Publication scores those predictions and appends transfer_ok or transfer_failed to each cited finding.
- KB skill is 1 - Brier_KB / Brier_base-rate. A finding earns 'transferable' only by predicting correctly on a new substrate.
- Failure classes are knowledge too. They live as executable checks with corpus fixtures, and their generalization is the checker's held-out incident recall.
- Pointers stay current mechanically. PTR-04 forces any pointer quoting a narrowed finding to cite the narrowing row, so the layer agents read first carries the latest caveat (the P036 +22.10pp case).

**Deliberately not built:** generated CATALOG and MEMO views, a hypothesis lifecycle, operation-signature alias tables, and prose claim-citation lint. The findings ledger, generated headlines, pointer copies and scored predictions address the same failures at about a tenth of the upkeep.
designs.rigorous_testing_loop:
**The user's loop, mapped onto fail-closed points.** Every layer tests the layer below it.

- **Explore and search.** The agent reads DELIVERY_LEDGER (E3 cadence, G series), FINDINGS (active and narrowed) and open INCIDENTS. The lock must cite basis findings and register predictions (LOCK-09, LOCK-11). Candidate selection itself stays judgment.
- **Design.** ENDPOINT_LOCK.json carries the contract's five-item block as fields: objective_distance, an unconditional own-EOS primary with an absolute floor, and the analytic input SNR. gate --stage lock then checks closure, purity, isolation and timing.
- **Refinement and audit, as cycle 0, before learner code.** Two things are measured on the exact split and code:
  - testbed validity: the ceiling learner passes and frozen random features fail;
  - the analytic SNR.
  If either fails, the verdict is CANNOT_TEST_CLAIM_AS_SPECIFIED.
- **Test run 1 (technical).** One technical record per arm produces receipts and ADMISSION.json. gate --stage roster runs the control differential from raw receipts, directional fixtures at production parameters, gates with demonstrated FAIL and PASS, input contrast, taught acquisition above the best shortcut, SHUF band and exposure. The same gate runs the reducer mutation suite RED-01..09 on verdict.py against synthetic rows, so the gate is tested before any data exist.
- **Test run 2 (dev).** Produces dev OUTPUTS.jsonl. score --role dev runs the shortcut ladder and the substitution test (the rule must fail with the candidate replaced by the best shortcut), plus comparator strength and strata. Any outcome-informed endpoint change becomes an amendment with an owner decision.
- **Test run 3 (rehearsal).** gate --stage official --dry, plus the tier-2 review: the other agent executes checks, attempts the cheapest shortcut, and runs canary mutations seeded with its own fresh seed, all of which must be caught.
- **Official run.** gate --stage official: everything above, plus AUTHORIZATION caps, a lock pushed or attested, and world freshness when the claim will be SEALED_CONFIRM.
- **Audit and search.** score --role official, then claim, then gate --stage publish and, if needed, --stage pointer. Predictions are scored, findings appended and incidents filed.

**Test-the-tests layers:**
- **L1, delivery gates.** Each gate needs a demonstrated FAIL on a negative fixture at production parameters and a PASS on an oracle (ADM-GATE, ADM-FIX). The decision rule must pass nine fail-closed fixtures (RED). The rule must reject the best shortcut (LAD-02).
- **L2, the checker.** A regression corpus of 20 synthetic fixtures, one per costly historical incident, with clean fixtures that must pass, so that blocking legitimate work also counts as a failure. selftest runs before any gate whenever the checker sha changes.
- **L3, held-out.**
  - Reviewer-seeded mutation canaries on each tier-2 delivery's own artifacts. The executor cannot know which arm, item, parameter or k will be mutated.
  - Held-out incident recall on incidents never used to build the checker (pre-Full151 archive, future discoveries).
- **L4, loop level.** Scored predictions against a base-rate forecaster, and sealed-world G as the only progress series.

**Anti-reward-hacking at the learner level.**
- Shortcut ladder: constant, frequency, exact and canonical key, copy-operand, fixed-length-k, mode-repeat.
- Trivial-strata exclusion.
- answer_path must be native.
- Exposure intersection.
- Native purity scan for backprop or attention.

**Anti-reward-hacking at the research-agent level.**
- Lock before look.
- Amendments recorded with the results already seen.
- Generated claims.
- No hand-written measurements.
- Checker sha verification.
- Protected paths with owner decisions.
- Canaries.
- An honest exit with no penalty.
