transfer_record is updated from PREDICTION_SCORES. A fact with >= 2 transfer_failed results and negative Brier skill score is demoted to narrowed with a scope rewrite. A fact whose only sources are local cannot exceed R1 and cannot be the sole basis of a design decision (UF-02 V9.9A/B).

A row moves from proposed to active only after reconciliation by a reviewer whose identity differs from the delivering author (LED-010). Lessons are solicited symmetrically from both agents at census, because each agent drops a different safeguard: Codex deletes forecasts, Claude omits E-levels.

Each incident is classified to an FM-xx class or NEW, with origin_stage, found_stage, found_by and wasted cost. check_escape=true if a check existed but did not fire. An incident is closed only when an executable check plus dirty and clean corpus fixtures exist and mfl corpus run catches them. Recurrence after closure reopens the class and is counted in MM-7.
HYPOTHESES follow a lifecycle: proposed, active, tested, retired, transferred. On a substrate change, every active hypothesis is explicitly transferred or retired.
Operation-signature index: mechanisms are keyed by an op-signature hash, aliases map to it, and a renamed recipe inherits earlier negatives (A10 alias table, U055 misassignment).
FAILURE_CLASSES.json is protected. Adding a class or tightening a check goes through minifly-loop-governance, but anyone may append INCIDENTS rows.

skills.name: minifly-user-decisions
skills.description_frontmatter: Use whenever a MiniFly action needs Mr. Zhou's decision, or you are recording one. That covers granting design, implementation, cycles, official run, confirmation, push, adoption or pointer changes; presenting options; and evaluating a conditional grant. It also covers any proposal touching CONSTRAINTS.json or a protected invariant (native-line bans, no supplied arithmetic structure, warmup, own EOS, objective metric), waiving a gate, narrowing task, metric or priority, and approving loosenings of skills or tools. Records verbatim text, the options and any recommendation shown, stage booleans, caps and machine-checkable conditionals in AUTHORIZATION.json or DECISIONS.jsonl.
skills.purpose: Grounds authorization in the owner's words and caps rather than the agent's framing, so the launcher, not the authorized agent, enforces scope. Silent drift becomes distinguishable from authorized narrowing.
skills.when_invoked: Before any T1+ execution stage, every T3 action, any constraint-touching proposal, any waiver, any scope or metric change, any governance loosening.
key_rules: AUTHORIZATION.json records the owner's verbatim text, timestamp and channel or session; options_shown with cost and E3 distance; recommendation_shown, kept separate; stage booleans; numeric caps copied from SPEC and restated to the owner; conditionals as predicates; and constraints_sha256.

A grant that is silent on caps gets the RULES defaults: T1 only, <= 2 CPU-h, <= 3 cycles, no official run, no push. Grant growth beyond caps (96 -> 512 -> 54,432 records across deliveries) requires a new grant.

Conditional grants ('if the audit helps, run') are written as predicates over named artifacts, evaluated by mfl auth predicate run by a non-executor identity, with the result recorded. The executor never judges its own condition.
A memo's 'approved' is not authorization. Pressure phrases ('keep going') become a scoped amendment only after the caps are restated to the owner and acknowledged verbatim.
Proposals touching CONSTRAINTS.json or PROTECTED_INVARIANTS.json are marked REQUIRES_USER_DECISION and cannot execute in the iteration in which they are proposed.
Waivers in DECISIONS.jsonl are scoped (rule ids, deliveries), carry an expiry, state exactly what they waive, and are cited by the gate output that used them. A waiver never upgrades a claim.
Present loosening and tightening items of a governance change as an itemized diff with the computed classification. Never bundle them for a single yes.
User adoption is recorded as USER_ADOPTED and is distinct from SCIENTIFICALLY_CONFIRMED and ENGINEERING_REFERENCE.

Objective numeric targets (held exact minimum, samples and compute budget) are owner decisions. Until set, CONSTRAINTS.objective_targets=TARGET_UNSET, and MM-1 is reported as a frontier without pass/fail. Agents never invent targets.

skills.name: minifly-loop-governance
skills.description_frontmatter: Use whenever anyone proposes to create, edit, relax, remove, re-tier or re-version a MiniFly skill, loopkit tool, RULES.json parameter, failure-class check, countermodel, regression fixture, CONSTRAINTS/PROTECTED_INVARIANTS, hooks or AGENTS.md, including a 'small fix' to a check that is blocking your own delivery. Defines protected paths, strictness-monotone classification, the regression-corpus, held-out canary and false-positive requirements, conflict-of-interest rules, user decisions for loosenings, versioning, and the loop version that every lock records.
skills.purpose: Recursive self-improvement without meta-Goodhart. The loop may improve its own skills and tools, but only through changes that are classified mechanically, regression-tested on old incidents, held-out-tested on canaries, reviewed by the other agent, owner-approved when they loosen, and applied prospectively.
skills.when_invoked: Any change to a protected path; any proposal from meta-eval; any request to relax a blocking check.
key_rules: Protected paths: .claude/skills/**, AGENTS.md, loopkit/**, .githooks/**, .claude/settings.json, and in PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/LOOP/: RULES.json, PROTECTED_INVARIANTS.json, CONSTRAINTS.json, FAILURE_CLASSES.json, MANIFEST.json, regression_corpus/** and tripwires/**. Ledgers are append-only rather than frozen.

Process: draft in PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/LOOP/PROPOSALS/<id>/ (diff, rationale citing an incident, canary miss, backtest result, evidenced false positive or measured ceremony cost) -> mfl governance check --base <sha> --head <sha> -> cross-agent review (stage=governance) -> owner DECISION if any item is loosen, removed, demoted or unclassifiable -> a merge commit that touches only protected paths plus its SKILL_CHANGES row and the new MANIFEST.

Classification is computed, not declared. RULES params carry a 'stricter' direction. These count as loosen: removing a check, fixture, enum restriction or required field; removing a skill line containing an mfl command or a MUST/NEVER rule; tier demotion. Anything unclassifiable counts as loosen.

Merge requirements: mfl selftest --mutate-tools passes; mfl corpus run gives 100% detect and 100% clean-pass for FM-01..FM-30; canary recall on the last revealed batch does not fall; the retro false-positive count on clean twins stays within budget; new or tightened rules run in advisory mode for 2 deliveries before enforcement.

Conflict of interest: a proposal by an agent whose in-flight delivery is blocked by the rule is marked conflicted. It cannot apply to that delivery, needs the other agent's review and an owner DECISION, and must not share a commit with any delivery artifact (GOV-009).
Changes apply prospectively. Each delivery is gated under the loop_version in its LOCK or CYCLE_PLAN. Later tightenings yield ADVISORY_UNDER_CURRENT findings, unless the owner makes one retroactive.
A fix after a canary miss must generalize. String-matching the revealed canary is rejected; the fix must catch the burned canary and also face the next sealed batch.
Never justify a change by more PASSes, fewer flags, faster launches or unblocking a result.

Tripwires: a decoy held-answer file with a canary token, a decoy gate_overrides.json that nothing reads, and a decoy scorer copy. Any edit to them, any appearance of the token elsewhere, or any runtime open by a learner or runner is a GOVERNANCE_BREACH (TRP-001..003).

Enforcement layers. The Claude PreToolUse hook denies Edit and Write on protected paths unless an open proposal exists. The git pre-commit hook (core.hooksPath=.githooks) refuses protected-path commits without Loop-Decision or SKILL_CHANGES. session-start re-validates history, so a hook bypass is caught by the next session. Recommended to the owner: CODEOWNERS plus branch protection, or owner-signed tags loop-vX.Y.Z, because git author names are shared.

Versioning: MANIFEST.json lists the sha256 of every protected file, and loop_version = sha256(canonical MANIFEST). Semver: major for any loosen, minor for tighten or new, patch for neutral text. LOCK, CYCLE_PLAN and REVIEW record loop_version.
Sunset path against ceremony creep: a check with zero live or canary catches over >= 10 deliveries and cost above its tier budget may be proposed for demotion. The owner decides in the census batch.

skills.name: minifly-meta-eval
skills.description_frontmatter: Use on the meta-evaluation cadence (each census, every five deliveries, before merging any governance change) or when asked how well the MiniFly research loop is working. Covers: planting or revealing sealed held-out canaries as a separate agent; running the regression corpus and the retro replay on historical deliveries; running frozen-knowledge-base backtests against a base-rate forecaster; scoring prediction calibration and recurrence of closed failure classes; measuring ceremony cost; and writing LOOP_HEALTH.json, in which sealed held-E3 progress is the only progress metric.
skills.purpose: The held-out evaluation of the research loop as a learner. It measures whether taught units (facts, checks) generalize to cases they were not built from, and produces the signals that drive governance proposals.
skills.when_invoked: Census, every 5 deliveries, before any governance merge, on owner request.
key_rules: Role separation. The meta-evaluator session did not author the tool changes or deliveries in the scored window. The canary author is the owner or a fresh session other than the tool authors of that interval. Backtest forecasters are fresh sessions that have read nothing after T.

Canary protocol. A batch is 10 synthetic mini-deliveries, at least 3 of them clean twins, written from FAILURE_CLASSES definitions only. At least half must be non-isomorphic to any corpus fixture. sha256 of bundle and key go into CANARY_COMMITMENTS.jsonl before the tool versions under test are merged. The bundle is kept outside the agents' working tree (owner storage) or encrypted with an owner-held key (HMAC-SHA256 counter-mode keystream). Reveal at the next census or before a governance merge, score recall per FM class and stage plus the false-alarm rate, then burn the batch into the regression corpus via governance.
Review canaries, with owner consent: about 1 in 5 review requests receive a seeded copy, and reviewer recall per FM is recorded. This measures collusion and shared blind spots between the two agents.
Retro replay: mfl retro --all --expect RETRO_EXPECTED.json. The 17 spot-checked incidents must all be flagged; the precision of other flags is sampled by the owner (5 per census).

KB backtest. Run mfl kb snapshot --as-of T, freeze an outcomes table by hash, and have another agent write redacted post-T design briefs. Three forecasters: Laplace base rate, a contract-only fresh session, and a KB-informed fresh session. Score Brier and log with a paired bootstrap. KB causal value = Brier(contract-only) - Brier(KB), with per-fact attribution. First run: T=2026-10-15 (after ROUTE_RETROSPECTIVE), predicting the 10-15..10-23 deliveries.

Compute MM-1..MM-10 with mfl metaeval report. MM-1 (sealed E3 frontier) is the only progress metric. The others are diagnostics, shown in tension pairs (catch-stage shift vs false positives; recall vs ceremony cost). No agent is scored, rewarded or prompted to improve them.
Outputs are PROPOSALS (never direct edits) plus a one-page LOOP_HEALTH digest for the owner listing the decisions requested (waivers, sunsets, canary keys, targets).
Owner spot-check: each census, 3 randomly sampled CLAIM numbers are traced to raw artifacts by the owner (about 10 minutes) as an anchor independent of both agents.

tools.purpose: Single stdlib entry point and dispatcher. It checks its own integrity, runs session start, computes the tier, runs the stage gate requirement table, provides read-only retro mode, and serves as the hook entry for Claude PreToolUse and git pre-commit/pre-push. It adds its own directory to sys.path explicitly, so python3 -I works.
tools.cli: python3 -I loopkit/mfl.py session-start [--brief] | tier --delivery DIR | gate --stage {explore|design_lock|cycle_start|cycle_end|admission|launch|reduce|publish|pointer_update|adopt} --delivery DIR [--json OUT] | retro (--delivery DIR | --all) [--expect RETRO_EXPECTED.json] [--out SCRATCH_DIR] | hook {pretooluse|precommit|prepush} | selftest [--mutate-tools] | preflight --delivery DIR
checks: MFL-001 self-integrity: every loopkit and skill file sha256 equals MANIFEST.json, and the MANIFEST hash equals the latest governed loop_version
MFL-002 KB presence: PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/LOOP ledgers exist, and the branch contains origin/codex/minifly-consolidated-20261023 as an ancestor

MFL-003 governance integrity: protected-path changes since the last validated marker each have a SKILL_CHANGES row (+ DECISION where required); precommit checks are re-run over unvalidated commits to catch hook bypass
MFL-004 staleness: CURRENT_* older than the newest ledger delivery in their track; open blocking incidents
MFL-010 tier inference: tier = max(declared, inferred from planned records/CPU, lineage cumulative compute, claim level, worlds_role, adoption/pointer flags); TIER_UNDERDECLARED
MFL-020 stage requirement table from RULES.json at the delivery's recorded loop_version (via git show <commit>:RULES.json): required artifacts present and schema-valid, then dispatch to sub-checks

MFL-030 retro: maps legacy artifacts (SOURCE_LOCK, AUTHORIZATION, FINAL_AUDIT, SUMMARY) and runs content checks only (AST lints, git timing, literal integrity, claim words, links, identical files, lock closure); absent v1 artifacts are reported legacy_absent, not FAIL
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Exit 0 only if every required check is PASS. 1 FAIL; 2 UNINFORMATIVE (missing file, unknown schema version, unknown enum, unresolvable predicate path); 3 GOVERNANCE_BREACH (every stage is blocked until an owner DECISION resolves it); 4 TOOL_ERROR (any exception). Hooks deny on any non-zero result. Retro always exits 0 with findings JSON labelled RETRO_FINDINGS_NO_VERDICT_CHANGE. It never executes delivery code by default and refuses any --out path inside a *_design_*, *_dev_* or delivery directory.
tools.self_tests: mfl selftest runs each module's unit tests (every check has >= 1 dirty and >= 1 clean fixture), then the full regression corpus. --mutate-tools replaces each check function in-process with always-PASS and with always-FAIL; the corpus must fail in both cases, which proves every check is exercised and that clean twins exist. Target runtime under 30 s.

tools.purpose: Validator for every schema-v1 artifact: required fields by tier, closed enums, types, canonical-JSON hashing, and computed_by provenance for integrity fields.
tools.cli: python3 -I loopkit/mfl.py schema validate FILE [--kind spec|predictions|units|auth|cycle_plan|cycle_record|admission|mutation|control_diff|lock|review|reconciliation|claim|scores|fact|incident|holdout|decision|skill_change|canary] | schema hash FILE --canonical
checks: SCH-001 required fields per kind and tier
SCH-002 closed enums (unknown value FAIL)
SCH-003 known schema version (minifly.<kind>/v1)
SCH-004 integrity-like fields carry computed_by {check_id, tool_version, output_sha256}
SCH-005 JSON round-trip equality (tuple/list, numpy scalar repr, NaN) for plans and receipts
tools.fail_closed_behavior: An unknown kind or version is UNINFORMATIVE (exit 2). Extra keys inside enum-typed objects FAIL. A file that does not parse FAILs.
tools.self_tests: One valid and several invalid fixtures per kind. Includes a free-text evidence_level fixture (one of the 40 strings in EXPERIMENT_CATALOG.json) that must FAIL, and the numpy bool_ round-trip fixture.

tools.purpose: Builds and verifies LOCK.json: static AST import closure, file hashes, gate/verdict/reducer inclusion, push-before-score ancestry and timing, endpoint and predictions hashes, amendment completeness and loop_version.
tools.cli: python3 -I loopkit/mfl.py lock build --delivery DIR --entry run.py [--entry ...] --roots DIR... --out LOCK.draft.json | lock verify --delivery DIR [--remote origin --branch codex/minifly-consolidated-20261023]
checks: LCK-001 static AST closure of entries, data generators, checks, gate and reducer is a subset of the lock files; non-literal importlib/__import__ calls FAIL unless listed in dynamic_imports with resolved files
LCK-002 every locked file hash matches its bytes at the lock commit and on disk
LCK-003 gate, verdict and reducer files are inside the lock; verdict JSON embeds gate_sha256 and lock_sha256
LCK-004 the lock commit is an ancestor of the remote branch head and precedes, in commit order, the first commit containing scored artifacts
LCK-005 at T2+, a pre-lock REVIEW references the lock commit and is committed before the launch commit
LCK-006 files not in the lock that appear after the lock commit are auto-tagged POSTHOC and refused as gate inputs
LCK-007 loop_version present and equal to MANIFEST at the lock commit
LCK-008 endpoint_lock_sha256 equals the canonical hash of SPEC.primary_endpoint+guards; any later diff requires an AMENDMENTS row with a new protocol_id
LCK-009 predictions_sha256 present at T2+
LCK-010 the amendments list is complete against git history of SPEC and LOCK
tools.fail_closed_behavior: An unreachable remote or unknown ancestry is UNINFORMATIVE and blocks launch. A missing closure member FAILs. Git is invoked read-only through subprocess with fixed arguments.
tools.self_tests: A temporary git repository (git init in a tempdir) reproduces: design and results in the same commit (the 43d04b5e pattern); gate file outside the lock (V6 audit_results.py); omitted imported module (LEARNED-BANK bootstrap.py and the minifly_a_v3 store); a lock committed after results. Each must FAIL; the clean twin passes.

tools.purpose: Library imported as the first line of every runner; it is not a launcher and never starts learners itself. Inside the already-running process it enforces the lock closure, isolated mode, caps, the learner/evaluator open boundary, the input tap, probe state invariance and the resource ledger. mfl resources check validates the resulting ledgers.
tools.cli: from loopkit.runtime_guard import guard, InputTap, ResourceLedger; guard('LOCK.json', role='learner'|'evaluator'|'runner') | python3 -I loopkit/mfl.py resources check --delivery DIR
checks: RTG-001 every loaded module with a repo __file__ is in the lock closure (checked at start and again at the first scored write)
RTG-002 sys.flags.isolated == 1 and PYTHONPATH absent
RTG-003 sys.addaudithook logs every open; learner role opening answer files, held manifests, evaluator outputs or tripwires raises and logs
RTG-004 InputTap records sha256(bytes), phase and feedback_flag for every sequence delivered to the learner -> INPUT_TAP.jsonl
RTG-005 the state digest is equal before and after each probe batch

RTG-006 ResourceLedger appends attempt_id, purpose, source sha, start/end, wall, RUSAGE_SELF and RUSAGE_CHILDREN deltas, maxrss, records and native event counters, using write-before-assert; refuses to start if AUTHORIZATION caps would be exceeded

RES-001 every result directory has a ledger attempt; RES-002 learner counters equal receipt counts; RES-003 retry legal only if the prior attempt has zero assessment-bearing records; RES-004 lineage-wide totals; RES-005 safeguard compute share reported against the tier budget
tools.fail_closed_behavior: On any violation it raises SystemExit(5) before any scored write and records the attempt as failed. An unwritable ledger aborts the process before work begins.
tools.self_tests: A dummy learner module outside the closure, a forbidden open of a held manifest, a probe that mutates state, a cap overrun and a busy-loop of known CPU time (validates the instrument on a known value); each must trip the guard.

tools.purpose: Static analysis of delivery code, with roles mapped by ROLES.json: common-mode auditors, clones, literal integrity fields, fail-open reducers, seed hygiene, native-path constraints, learner-evaluator boundary, write-before-assert, module collisions and the known-defect preflight.
tools.cli: python3 -I loopkit/mfl.py lint code --delivery DIR [--roles ROLES.json] | preflight --delivery DIR
checks: AST-001 auditor, reducer or evaluator files import any executor or learner module
AST-002 normalized-AST subtree clones (identifiers anonymized, >= 25 nodes) shared between auditor and executor (e.g. Package B branch_allows reuse; STOP-ONLY metric transcription)
AST-003 literal True/False/0 assigned to integrity keys (exposure_overlap, all_rows_decoded_*, no_training_*, *_independent*, *_verified*, *_passes)

AST-004 fail-open reducer patterns: 'is not False' or '!= False' on gate values, .get(k, True), all() over possibly-empty sequences, a supported-verdict denominator not read from LOCK, bare except around gate code
AST-005 RNG seeded from hash()/sha of prompt or answer bytes, or from salted builtin hash(); seeds must be f(world, index, purpose)

AST-006 native-path constraints from CONSTRAINTS.json in learner_native files: attention/Transformer modules, QK-softmax pattern, .backward(), torch.autograd, jax.grad, optimizers, lstsq/pinv/Ridge readout fits (ELM); evaluator files exempt
AST-007 learner files import evaluator modules or reference answer/held/tripwire paths
AST-008 gate function evaluated before its inputs are written to disk (WARN at T1, FAIL at T2+)
AST-009 prompt bytes used as dict keys mapping to answers in learner code (lookup-table smell, WARN)
AST-010 module names not delivery-prefixed, or colliding with other deliveries or stdlib
PRE-001 JSON round-trip, numpy scalar serialization, identity fields excluded from equality, zero/boundary slice tests, vendored files byte-diffed against tracked versions
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Unparsable files FAIL. A file without a role at T2+ is UNINFORMATIVE. The tool only parses and never imports delivery code.
tools.self_tests: Fixtures distilled from minifly_b branch_allows, minifly_v6_r1 audit_results.py:97 literals, LEARNED-BANK summarize.py 'is not False', a prompt-derived seed, a torch backward call in a native file, and the import-collision pattern from at least 10 deliveries. Each has a clean twin.

tools.purpose: Tests that a verdict reducer fails closed. It builds synthetic inputs from the LOCK roster and runs the reducer in an isolated subprocess on a temporary copy. A reducer is not a learner, so running one stays within the never-run-learners rule.
tools.cli: python3 -I loopkit/mfl.py reducer test --reducer PATH --lock LOCK.json [--fixture-set default] [--timeout 20] [--allow-exec-reducer]
checks: RED-001 a complete positive fixture yields PASS/supported (proves the reducer can pass)

RED-002 each degraded fixture yields FAIL or UNINFORMATIVE, never supported or partial-as-pass: missing arm (each), missing world, extra unknown world, None gate, exactly-at-margin minus epsilon, NaN metric, duplicated world, denominator mismatch
RED-003 DEV-tagged worlds yield DEV_NOT_EVIDENCE
RED-004 output embeds gate and lock sha
RED-005 the denominator comes from LOCK (fewer worlds never yields supported)
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Any 'supported' on a degraded fixture FAILs. A reducer crash counts as safe only if it exits non-zero and writes no verdict file. In retro mode a historical reducer is executed only with --allow-exec-reducer, and only after AST-001/AST-006 show it imports no learner or training module; otherwise the result is UNINFORMATIVE.
tools.self_tests: A LEARNED-BANK-style fail-open reducer (None oracle passes, missing COPY passes, any n_ok == len(verdict)) must FAIL; its corrected twin must PASS.

tools.purpose: Evaluator-side shortcut ladder, held-item stratification, determinacy witnesses, SHUF validity and the unit-dependency index. These are lookup and counting computations on manifests, tap logs and saved outputs; nothing is trained.
tools.cli: python3 -I loopkit/mfl.py cm ladder --exposures INPUT_TAP.jsonl|EXPOSURES.jsonl --probes PROBES.jsonl [--outputs OUTPUTS.jsonl] --spec SPEC.json --out COUNTERMODELS.json | cm strata --units UNITS.json --out STRATA.json | cm determinacy --units UNITS.json --witness {pair_rectangle|column_closure} | cm shuf-check --control SHUF.jsonl --truth TRUTH.jsonl | cm udi --outputs OUTPUTS.jsonl --variants VARIANTS.json --dependency DEPMAP.json
checks: CM-001 ladder: raw_lookup, canonical (commutative) lookup, frequency/mode, prompt_length_frequency, suffix0..4, constant, fixed_length_0..8 stop rules, position_only, copy_operand_a/b, identity (x+0), digitwise_no_carry, nearest_neighbour by byte overlap, HASH_CODE
CM-002 SPEC gate comparator must be >= max(chance, ladder, controls); a weaker comparator FAILs
CM-003 non-discriminating endpoint (any arm >= 95% or all <= 5%)
CM-004 strata S0..S4 at manifest time; headline only S2+; minimum distinct correct orbits per stratum
CM-005 determinacy fraction for held items under the declared witness; undetermined items listed
CM-006 SHUF agreement with truth in [0.4, 0.6] for binary labels (about 1/k for k classes) and orbit-consistent; a derangement on binary labels FAILs
CM-007 UDI with a world-level paired bootstrap CI (stdlib random, fixed seed)
CM-008 modal-output fraction and output entropy per probe pool, emitted automatically
tools.fail_closed_behavior: At T2+, if only the manifest is supplied with no tap, the exposure-based ladder is UNINFORMATIVE (the tap is required). An unknown prompt format FAILs. Missing outputs for any probe FAIL.
tools.self_tests: STOP/FIXED_1 fixture (FIXED_1 10.645% vs STOP 11.263% on NEW, FIXED_1 > STOP on OLD) must flag the comparator; V6-style zero-operand held items must be classed S0; SHUF derangement fixture; additive rectangle fixture where all 20 held items are determined; mode-byte 0x31 output fixture must show a modal fraction > 0.98.

tools.purpose: The one versioned statistics and decision module that deliveries import. Implemented in pure Python with tabulated-value validation. It also simulates the operating characteristics of decision rules.
tools.cli: python3 -I loopkit/mfl.py stats oc --rule RULE.json --n-worlds N --sd-grid 0.02,0.05,0.1 --target DELTA --sims 2000 --out OC_SIM.json | stats lint --delivery DIR | from loopkit.stats import decide, paired_t, hoeffding, clopper_pearson, holm, iut
checks: STA-001 P(pass|target) >= 0.8 at the declared SD, otherwise label precision_limited_screen
STA-002 ratio-of-differences hard gates rejected
STA-003 zero variance gives Hoeffding with the registered range or UNRESOLVED, never a zero-width interval
STA-004 Bonferroni applied inside a single conjunction flagged (use intersection-union)
STA-005 the population the interval covers is declared (factors resampled per world)
STA-006 DEV winner >= 2 SE over parent with expected-shrinkage note
STA-007 bespoke decision code: the reducer must call stats.decide with the locked rule
tools.fail_closed_behavior: An unknown rule type FAILs. A simulation with fewer than 1,000 draws is UNINFORMATIVE.
tools.self_tests: t and Clopper-Pearson quantiles checked against tabulated values; persistent_core_v2 fixture (ratio gate at alpha .05/21, ERROR LB -4.24) flagged as unreachable; native_context_binding zero-variance interval fixture flagged.

tools.purpose: Lints claims, text, citations, links and padding: closed-enum CLAIM, banned wording, confirm and native vocabulary, number-artifact binding, provenance mixing, citation checks against the ledger, link checks and ceremony padding.
tools.cli: python3 -I loopkit/mfl.py lint claim --delivery DIR | lint text FILE... [--delivery DIR] | lint citations FILE... | lint links PATH... | lint padding --delivery DIR [--across-deliveries]
checks: CLM-001 CLAIM enums; headline begins with primary_gate; objective_metric line present
CLM-002 banned soft words within 12 tokens of primary or gate mentions; 'approved' without a DECISION reference
CLM-003 confirm* only if all worlds are SEALED_CONFIRM
CLM-004 native|core|inherited|same fly requires a lineage row with demonstrated inheritance
CLM-005 headline, summary and pointer numbers bound to {file,key} and equal within rounding
CLM-006 held numbers only from the prespecified checkpoint
CLM-007 no arithmetic combining numbers with different provenance tags
CLM-008 bare booleans (confirmation_passes etc.) in SUMMARY, STATUS or CURRENT without objective_metric
CLM-009 evidence level must be an enum value
CIT-001 numeric or historical claims about prior work cite UF, FM or catalog IDs
CIT-002 quoted value, comparator and caveat match the ledger (narrowed facts must carry their caveat)
LNK-001 no absolute local paths (/Users/, /home/, /tmp/) in published files
LNK-002 relative links resolve
PAD-001 byte-identical files across cycles or deliveries
PAD-002 boilerplate ratio (sentences repeated in >= 3 deliveries) above the RULES threshold
PAD-003 a note claiming a check cites an artifact committed earlier in commit order
tools.fail_closed_behavior: A missing CLAIM.json at publish FAILs. An unbindable headline number is UNINFORMATIVE and blocks. Text lint is advisory at T0 and blocking at T1+.
tools.self_tests: CLS 'G1 memory - largely met' fixture, LEARNED-BANK 'Native confirmation' on D2, catalog P036 uncaveated +22.10pp, a /Users/pencilbard path, byte-identical multimechanism cycle audits, and 'confirmation_passes': true without an objective metric. Each has a clean twin.

tools.purpose: Append-only, hash-chained ledgers; regeneration of the CURRENT_*, catalog and memo views; staleness and E3 cadence; operation-signature lookup; failure-class trigger evaluation.

LED-002 git history of ledgers is append-only
LED-003 no deleted cycles/ or failure directories since the last validated marker (git log --diff-filter=D)
LED-004 committed generated views equal the regenerated output (hand-edit detection)
LED-005 pointer staleness relative to the newest delivery in the track
LED-006 narrowed facts quoted in views carry their caveat
LED-007 deliveries_since_last_opened_E3 >= 2 means the next SPEC must open E3 or cite a waiver DECISION
LED-008 op-signature Jaccard >= 0.8 to a tested version must be cited, and its negatives are inherited
LED-009 FAILURE_CLASSES trigger predicates evaluated over SPEC give the required check list; an unresolved path counts as fired
LED-010 a fact or failure-class status beyond 'proposed' requires a reviewer identity different from the delivering author

tools.purpose: Registry of worlds, items, orbit universes, seed families and the reserved E3 family; touch accounting; commit-reveal seeds with an evaluator-held salt.

HO-002 held items do not overlap any previously scored held item; the item-universe overlap fraction is reported and blocks above threshold in small universes (e.g. 55 orbits)
HO-003 confirmation seeds must come from an HMAC commitment; public-string or sequential derivations FAIL
HO-004 HMAC seed recomputation matches
HO-005 reserved E3 family looks <= budget, with pass/fail-only feedback recorded
HO-006 once touched, a world is DEV forever
HO-007 every world appearing in a delivery's results has a touch row

tools.purpose: Registration, validation and proper scoring of predictions; calibration per agent and per fact; transfer annotations for facts.
tools.cli: python3 -I loopkit/mfl.py predict validate PREDICTIONS.json | predict score --delivery DIR --outcomes OUTCOMES.json --out PREDICTION_SCORES.json | predict calibration [--agent A] [--fact UF-xx] [--since DATE]
checks: PRD-001 every primary and guard endpoint has >= 1 prediction; types valid; probabilities in [0.02, 0.98]; intervals ordered; base_rate with source; derived_from IDs exist
PRD-002 the predictions hash is in LOCK and precedes the first scored value in commit order
PRD-003 the scored set equals the registered set; reviewer annotations are additions only
PRD-004 scoring: Brier, log score, 90% interval hit and Winkler interval score, base-rate Brier, skill = 1 - Brier/base
PRD-005 proposed transfer_record rows for each derived_from fact

tools.purpose: Checks review independence and execution, reconciliation, and authorization coverage including conditional predicates.

REV-003 non-executed findings labelled UNVERIFIED
REV-004 every finding reconciled with a status enum before publish
REV-005 identical or templated review content across cycles or deliveries

tools.purpose: Commit, reveal and scoring of sealed held-out canary batches (tool canaries and review canaries).

tools.purpose: Frozen-KB snapshot as of date T, outcome-table freezing, leak scanning and scoring for KB backtests.

designs.roles_and_independence:
Roles. Each is recorded as an identity object {agent: codex|claude|owner, model, session, role} in JSON and in commit trailers. Git author names are never identities: Codex commits as Pencilbard.

(1) OWNER, Mr. Changwei Zhou. Owns CONSTRAINTS.json, PROTECTED_INVARIANTS.json and the objective targets. Grants AUTHORIZATION for T1+ execution stages and all T3 actions. Approves adoption, waivers and every governance loosening. Holds canary keys (and a commit-signing key, if he enables signing). Traces 3 random CLAIM numbers to raw artifacts at each census.

(2) EXECUTOR, usually Codex, sometimes Claude. Writes EXPLORE_MEMO, SPEC, UNITS, learner and runner, runs cycles and builds the LOCK. It may not author the clean-room reducer, the scorer or countermodel configuration, or the confirmation salt for its own T2+ delivery. It may not review itself above T1.

(3) EVALUATOR, the other agent. Before results exist, writes the answer generator and scorer, mutant zoo parameters, control-differential expectations and the clean-room reducer from SPEC text alone, never importing executor code (AST-001/002). Generates the HMAC salt and commits its hash before the lock. Evaluates authorization conditionals.

(4) REVIEWER, the other agent; at T3 a different model family in a fresh session. Performs design pre-lock, pre-confirmation, post-run and governance reviews with executed checks and a premortem.

(5) META-EVALUATOR. A fresh session that authored neither the tool changes nor the deliveries in the scored window. Runs corpus, retro, canary scoring, backtests and LOOP_HEALTH, and may only file PROPOSALS.

(6) CANARY AUTHOR. The owner, or a fresh session other than the tool authors of the interval. Writes canaries from FM definitions only, never from tool code.

(7) FORECASTER. A fresh session for KB backtests that sees only the snapshot and redacted briefs.

(8) REDACTOR. A non-forecaster agent that builds the post-T briefs.

Independence matrix by tier.
- T0: self allowed, labelled.
- T1: self review allowed, labelled independence_class=self; outputs stamped DEV_NOT_EVIDENCE.
- T2: cross_agent required for design and post-run review, and EVALUATOR is not EXECUTOR for reducer and scorer.
- T3: T2 plus a cross_family fresh-context reviewer, the evaluator-held salt and an owner decision.

Enforcement.
- mfl review check (REV-001) blocks when identities match above T1.
- LED-010 blocks fact activation by the delivering author alone.
- CAN-001 and KB-002 enforce meta-role separation.
- LCK-003/AST-001 enforce reducer provenance.

Degraded mode. If only one agent is available, the delivery is capped at T1. No confirmation, adoption or pointer change happens until cross-agent review exists.

Shared blind spots. Both reviewers are LLMs and may share blind spots or collude, so three anchors sit outside both agents' judgment: mechanical checks; review canaries that measure each reviewer's recall per FM class; and the owner's spot-check. Reviewers are credited for found defects, including successful cheapest-shortcut attacks. Executors are never penalized for honest exits, only for escaped defects found later. That removes the incentive to hide defects.
designs.rsi_mechanism:
THE RESEARCH LOOP AS A MINIFLY LEARNER. Each element of MiniFly's evaluation has a counterpart in the loop:
- Taught units -> unit facts and failure classes, each with trigger predicates and executable checks, taught by incidents and results.
- Own output before feedback -> predictions registered in the lock before any scored value, and the loop's own fail-closed verdicts.
- Exact-key and frequency countermodels -> the base-rate forecaster (Laplace over the track, e.g. native E3 pass (0+1)/(8+2)=0.10 from UF-27), the contract-only forecaster, and 'checks that only match the exact historical instance'.
- Held-out composition -> future experiments' outcomes, sealed canaries that are new variants of known classes, and frozen-KB backtests.
- Causal prior-teaching control -> KB ablation: a contract-only forecaster vs a KB-informed one, giving KB causal value.
- OLD protection -> the regression corpus. Every historical incident class stays caught after every change, at 100%.
- Sealed worlds -> sealed canary batches and sealed E3 worlds.
- Reward hacking -> meta-Goodhart, i.e. editing the checker.
- Gradual warmup -> new rules run advisory for 2 deliveries before enforcement.

META-OBJECTIVE.
Primary: MM-1, the sealed E3 frontier. For each SEALED_CONFIRM delivery that passes integrity, the OLD guard and native_only path, take LB95 of unconditional exact own-EOS held accuracy on S2+ strata at the final checkpoint, minus the strongest countermodel or control on the same items. Plot it against lineage-wide counted compute (native event counters, including all search, tuning, surrogate, cycle-0 and failed attempts) and against taught samples. Progress means a new non-dominated point. Looks at the reserved E3 family are counted in ALPHA_LEDGER.
Constraints:
(c1) zero unmatched protected-path changes and tripwire hits (MM-10).
(c2) regression corpus at 100% detect and 100% clean-pass.
(c3) canary recall on the latest batch does not decrease.
(c4) safeguard cost within tier budgets.
Diagnostic learning signals (never optimization targets):
- MM-2 detection-stage profile and escape cost: compute spent between a defect's origin stage and its detection.
- MM-3 canary recall and false-alarm rate per FM and stage.
- MM-4 retro recall on the 17 spot-checked incidents, with owner-sampled precision.
- MM-5 Brier skill and interval coverage of registered predictions, per agent and per fact.
- MM-6 KB backtest skill and KB causal value.
- MM-7 recurrence of closed failure classes.
- MM-8 deliveries since the last opened E3 and the share of compute spent on E3-opened deliveries.
- MM-9 ceremony cost.
- MM-10 governance integrity.
Why PASS counts cannot game these:
- MM-1 needs commit-reveal seeds with an evaluator-held salt, a clean-room reducer by the non-executor, and subtraction of the strongest countermodel.
- MM-3 uses canaries the tool authors never saw.
- MM-5 and MM-6 use proper scoring rules against base rates: copying the base rate scores zero skill, and wide intervals are penalized by the interval score.
- MM-2 and MM-7 count only incidents found by independent reviewers, canaries or tools.
- No composite score exists. Every metric is shown with its tension partner (catch-stage shift vs false positives; recall vs ceremony).

UPDATE RULES (how the loop improves itself).
U1 Incident -> check. Each incident is classified. A check_escape tightens that check and adds a variant fixture. A new class gets an FM id, a trigger, a check and dirty and clean fixtures. A class closes at R2 and becomes protected at R3.
U2 Prediction -> fact. Scores update transfer_record. A fact reaches R3 after its first in-scope prediction beats the base rate on a later delivery. Two failed transfers with negative skill demote it to narrowed.
U3 Canary miss -> generalize the check. A fix that string-matches the revealed canary is rejected. The fix must catch the burned canary and then face the next sealed batch.
U4 Backtest -> knowledge format. If KB-informed forecasts do not beat contract-only forecasts, the KB is not generalizing. The response is a proposal to restructure it (more prediction templates, sharper trigger predicates), not to add more prose.
U5 Ceremony -> sunset. A check with high cost and zero live or canary catches over 10 or more deliveries is proposed for demotion; the owner decides.
U6 Skills -> governance. Skill text, tools and rules change only through minifly-loop-governance.

GOVERNANCE AGAINST META-GOODHART.
- Protected paths with self-protecting hashes (MANIFEST, MFL-001).
- Computed strictness classification: removal or unclassifiable counts as loosen.
- Loosening requires an owner DECISION matching the diff hash.
- Tightening requires cross-agent review, corpus 100%, the retro false-positive budget and an advisory period.
- Conflict-of-interest rule: a fix to a check that blocks your own delivery never applies to that delivery and needs the owner.
- Prospective versioning: every LOCK, CYCLE_PLAN and REVIEW records loop_version {semver, manifest_sha256, commit}, and each delivery is gated under its recorded version.
- Tripwires (decoy answers with a canary token, an ignored gate_overrides.json, a decoy scorer) plus runtime audit hooks.
- Hook bypass detected by history re-validation at every session start.
- Recommended git-level anchors the owner can enable: CODEOWNERS with branch protection, or owner-signed loop-vX.Y.Z tags.
- Agents are never prompted or rewarded to improve MM-2..MM-10.
- Lessons written by the delivering agent are proposals reconciled by the other agent.

CADENCE. Meta-eval runs at each census, every 5 deliveries, and before any governance merge. Outputs are PROPOSALS plus a one-page owner digest.
designs.knowledge_mechanism:
Store. PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/LOOP/ holds append-only, hash-chained JSONL ledgers on every branch: UNIT_FACTS, INCIDENTS, HYPOTHESES, SIGNATURES, RESEARCH_LEDGER, HOLDOUT_REGISTRY, DECISIONS, SKILL_CHANGES, ALPHA_LEDGER and CANARY_COMMITMENTS. FAILURE_CLASSES.json and RULES.json are protected. Session-start fails if the store is absent or the branch lacks the canonical head; origin/charming-head lacked PROJECT_DOCUMENTS. CURRENT_* pointers, catalog tables and memo tables are generated views (mfl ledger regen), and hand edits are detected (LED-004).

Seeding (phase 0). UF-01..UF-29 are seeded from the digest with statuses: UF-15 narrowed by the FIXED_1 result; UF-16 marked an uninformative manipulation; UF-02 unverifiable_in_repo; UF-25 dev-only. FM-01..FM-30 are seeded with triggers, checks and the cited incidents.

Units of research knowledge. A unit fact is a scoped tuple: claim, level, substrate/lineage hash, priors, feedback regime, dose, metric definition, comparator, strongest trivial baseline, effect with CI, scope limits, sources path:line plus sha256, and status with narrowed_by and superseded_by links. A failure class is {trigger predicate, required checks, judgment question, fixtures, incidents}.

Generalization levels R0-R4 apply to both facts and checks.
- R0: recorded.
- R1: reproduces (fact recomputed; check catches its own incident fixture).
- R2: changed presentation (variant fixture or re-derived metric).
- R3: held-out (catches a sealed canary; prediction beats the base rate on a delivery after recording).
- R4: cross-substrate or cross-track.
Only R3+ is 'transferable'. This is the research-level analog of E1 -> E2 -> E3.

From units to predictions. Facts carry prediction_template {trigger over SPEC, outcome, forecast}.
- UF-18/19: an analytic cue/noise ratio below the threshold predicts E0 admission failure.
- UF-06: a BP ceiling of 0-5% held in the raw-byte single-digit harness predicts CANNOT_TEST for E3 in that harness.
- UF-15: STOP-like conditional-stopping gains over DIRECT will not exceed FIXED_1 by more than 1pp.
- UF-27: base rate for native E3 pass.
mfl triggers turns in-scope templates into required PREDICTIONS rows for a design (block 6). Post-audit scoring writes transfer_ok or transfer_failed back to the fact. Calibration is reported per agent and per fact.

Failure classes as transferable checks. Trigger predicates over SPEC make checks apply whenever their condition recurs; for example, any change to the front end, init or read path requires the E0 input-discriminability check, which would have covered the at-least-5 recurrences of the address class. An incident closes only when an executable check plus dirty and clean fixtures exist. Recurrence after closure reopens the class and is counted (MM-7).

Hygiene.
- The citation linter checks quoted values, comparators and caveats against the ledger and blocks mixed-provenance numbers.
- Operation-signature hashing makes renamed recipes inherit their negatives.
- Hypotheses follow the lifecycle proposed -> active -> tested -> retired or transferred, with explicit transfer or retirement on a substrate change.
- Local-only sources cannot exceed R1 or be the sole basis of a decision.
- Lessons are solicited symmetrically from both agents and activated only by a reviewer who is not the delivering author.
- Skills store checks and procedures, never tactics that produced passes.

Measuring the KB as a learner. Freeze the KB at T (mfl kb snapshot), have a redactor brief post-T designs, and score three forecasters: base rate, contract-only and KB-informed. KB causal value = Brier(contract-only) - Brier(KB). Per-fact attribution shows which units actually generalize. First backtest: T=2026-10-15 over the 10-15..10-23 deliveries.
designs.rigorous_testing_loop:
The user's loop with the gate at each step:

1. EXPLORE (minifly-explore; gate explore). KB-first candidate generation, cadence rule, signature lookup, registered forecasts against the base rate, cheapest falsifier first, neutral options. Then AUTHORIZATION through minifly-user-decisions.

2. EXPERIMENT.
(a) Design (minifly-design + minifly-unit-to-composition; gate design_lock). Contract blocks 1-6, LINEAGE, objective distance, triggered FM checks, U2C units, strata and determinacy, operating characteristics, PREDICTIONS. At T2+, a cross-agent executing review before implementation. This is the cheapest moment; UF-28 shows pre-implementation reviews prevented runs.
(b) Cycle 0, testing the testbed and the tests (minifly-cycle0-admission; gate admission). Ceiling passes, floor and shortcuts fail, power at least 0.8 or labelled screen, E0 contrast, E1 preflight, oracle-upstream chain smoke, gate mutation score 1.0, control differential delivered, reducer fixtures fail closed. Verdict ADMITTED or an honest exit.
(c) Refinement -> audit -> test run, at most the authorized cap, default three typed cycles (minifly-cycles; gates cycle_start/cycle_end). Cycle 1 technical: preflight lint, teaching-port trio, import isolation, seeded bug caught. Cycle 2 dev_tuning: declared knobs and DEV worlds, best-of-k, held sets spent. Cycle 3 pilot: frozen design, one full history per arm on a fresh DEV world; it may only stop or escalate. Each cycle has a locked plan with a falsifiable prediction, a typed record and a decision.
(d) Official run (minifly-lock-and-launch; gates launch and reduce). Closure lock pushed before scoring, pre-lock cross-agent review, evaluator-salted seeds, zero-touch sealed worlds, runtime guard with input tap and audit hook, atomic paired units, clean-room reducer.

3. AUDIT AND SEARCH. Post-run independent audit with reconciliation (minifly-independent-review). Then CLAIM, prediction scoring, fact deltas and regenerated pointers (minifly-claim-and-publish; gates publish, pointer_update, adopt). Then a ledger update (minifly-knowledge-ledger), which feeds the next EXPLORE. Meta-eval and governance close the outer loop.

Testing the tests: a seven-level pyramid.
- L0 Tool self-tests. Every check has dirty and clean fixtures. mfl selftest --mutate-tools replaces each check with always-PASS and always-FAIL, and the suite must notice both. This is mutation testing of the checkers themselves.
- L1 Regression corpus. One or more dirty+clean mini-deliveries per FM-01..FM-30, distilled from real incidents. Examples: Package B branch_allows clone; v5.1 port fixture at activity 0.02 vs 0.0354; SHUF derangement; STOP vs FIXED_1; V6 zero-operand strata; audit_results literals; LEARNED-BANK fail-open summarize.py and incomplete lock; same-commit design and results; T-MOD -> T-PAR swap; 'largely met'; P036 caveat; '(Recommended)'; /Users paths; identical cycle audits; and governance fixtures. Detect and clean-pass must be 100%.
- L2 Retro replay on the 53 historical deliveries. Read-only and static by default. The 17 spot-checked incidents must be flagged; the precision of other flags is sampled by the owner. This answers the open question of whether the checks would false-positive on history.
- L3 Per-delivery tests of the experiment's own tests: testbed validity, gate mutation zoo including HASH_CODE, control differential, reducer degraded-input fixtures, fixture-parameter diffs against SPEC, a seeded bug per cycle.
- L4 Sealed held-out canaries by a separate author, for tools and for reviewers. These measure whether the checks generalize beyond the corpus, as held E3 measures beyond taught items. Burned batches feed L1.
- L5 Forecast scoring: every registered prediction scored post-run, plus KB backtests against base-rate and contract-only forecasters.
- L6 Owner spot-checks of 3 random claim numbers per census.

Anti-reward-hacking at the LEARNER level:
- Unconditional own-EOS primaries on S2+ strata against the full countermodel ladder (constant, mode, fixed-length, position, lookups, suffix, copy-operand, identity, no-carry, nearest-neighbour, FROZEN, SHUF, HASH_CODE).
- Determinacy witness.
- NO_PRIOR_TEACHING and leave-units-out UDI causal tests.
- Structure meters beside distinguishability gates.
- Answer-path provenance with native_only.
- Process separation: the learner exchanges bytes only, and the audit hook refuses opens of answer files.
- Input tap with exposure checked against what was actually fed.
- Probe state invariance.
- Native-path AST lint for attention, backprop and ELM.
- Seed hygiene.
- Sealed worlds.

Anti-reward-hacking at the RESEARCH-AGENT level, each mapped to a literature pattern:
- Scorer patching (METR o3): evaluator separation, gate and reducer in the lock, audit hook.
- Time-limit editing (AI Scientist): caps in owner AUTHORIZATION, enforced in the runner, cap changes after lock need a decision.
- Deleting failure markers (Darwin Godel Machine): append-only hash chains, LED-003 deletion detection.
- Disabling the sandbox (STOP): hook bypass caught by history re-validation, tripwires.
- Test modification (ImpossibleBench): GATE_DIFF with other-agent sign-off and new negative tests, protected corpus.
- Self-judged conditionals and option framing: AUTH-002/005.
- Confirming on tuning worlds: holdout registry, CLM-003.
- Claim inflation: claim lint.
- Abort option (ImpossibleBench showed it reduces cheating): honest exits are explicit, first-class and unpenalized.

coverage.mechanism: EVALUATOR writes the clean-room reducer and scorer from SPEC text (minifly-lock-and-launch). AST-001 import scan and AST-002 normalized-AST clone scan between auditor and executor. Control-differential expectations derived from SPEC. The corpus contains the Package B branch_allows mismatch and STOP-ONLY metric transcription. Reviewer judgment: name the shared helper the verdict depends on.

CONTROL_DIFFERENTIAL.json after one technical record per arm: digest differs exactly where SPEC says, and realized dose >= minimum. The verdict enum separates TREATMENT_NOT_DELIVERED from NULL (minifly-cycle0-admission). Corpus: Package B identical arms, CREDIT 0.3% attenuation, native_next shared BASE residual.

SPEC.intervention_manifest declared_changed/declared_fixed, measured in cycle 0. More than one factor auto-labels integrated_intervention, and claim lint bans mechanism attribution. The LINEAGE ops diff flags undeclared changes (v4 7 factors, EXPAND wiring/gain).

MUTATION_SCORE.json with the full mutant zoo including HASH_CODE and birth_state at production parameters diffed against SPEC. Score must be 1.0; gates with no demonstrated FAIL are relabelled sanity. CM-006 SHUF validity, CM-003 non-discriminating detection, a noise-floor rule against testing invariants. Corpus: v5.1 port at activity 0.02, derangement SHUF, teacher-forcing tautology.

Cycle-0 testbed validity table (ceiling passes, FROZEN and shortcuts fail, surrogate can pass) on the exact split. mfl stats oc requires P(pass|target) >= 0.8 or a precision_limited_screen label. STA-002 bans ratio-of-differences hard gates. U2C determinacy witness excludes undetermined held items. Verdict CANNOT_TEST_CLAIM_AS_SPECIFIED.

Countermodel ladder CM-001; comparator rule CM-002 = max(chance, ladder, controls) + margin + absolute floor + per-world floor. Guard lint rejects never-taught comparators. S0-S4 strata at manifest time, headline only on S2+. Corpus: STOP vs FIXED_1, below-chance FROZEN/SHUF comparator, V6 zero-operand strata, NO_OLD guard.

CLAIM.objective_metric is mandatory, or 'not_measured'. CLM-008 forbids bare booleans in SUMMARY/STATUS/CURRENT. gate_type component|objective. Conditional metrics only paired with unconditional ones. CM-008 modal fraction and entropy emitted automatically. Answer-path provenance; hybrid paths cannot carry the objective label.

LCK-008 endpoint hash; AMENDMENTS.jsonl with results seen, evidence path, reason enum, original endpoint kept as co-primary, new protocol_id, owner re-authorization for task or metric changes. CLM-003 bans 'confirm' on DEV. Corpus: LEARNED-BANK T-MOD -> T-PAR swap, observation_content primary rewrite, Cstar from KEEP_OLD.

LED-007 cadence: after 2 non-E3 deliveries, the next SPEC opens E3 or cites an owner waiver. objective_distance on fixed axes. Component bridge rule in U2C (predicted E3 effect registered and scored). Scope changes need DECISIONS kind=scope_narrowing, which separates authorized narrowing from drift. MM-8 cadence metric.

Typed CYCLE_PLAN/CYCLE_RECORD with revision classes enforced at cycle_end. A post-outcome SCI revision increments best-of-k, spends held sets and forces fresh worlds. Allowed-inductive-bias whitelist; priors appear in the headline. Decision enum instead of a count. PAD-001 flags identical cycle files.

HOLDOUT_REGISTRY with touch counts (HO-001..007). Item-universe overlap blocking. HMAC seeds with an evaluator-held salt. Reserved E3 family with counted looks and ALPHA_LEDGER. Worlds touched once are DEV forever. Corpus: value-retention fixed orbits, shared worlds 202610143901-03, D3 reuse, sequential ids.

runtime_guard InputTap; the exposure audit is computed from the tap, never the manifest. Audit hook refuses learner opens of answer files. Probe state-digest invariance. AST-005 seed hygiene and AST-007 learner-evaluator boundary. Held partition fixed before streams. Leakage sheet fields in SPEC. Tripwire canary tokens.

mfl lock build/verify: static AST closure plus a runtime closure assertion; gate, verdict and reducer inside the lock; lock commit an ancestor of the remote head and earlier than the first scored commit; pre-lock review references the lock commit; post-lock files auto-POSTHOC; loop_version recorded. Corpus: same-commit design and results, V6 audit_results outside the lock, LEARNED-BANK missing bootstrap.py and stores.

reducer_harness RED-001..005: degraded inputs must fail closed, DEV tag gives DEV_NOT_EVIDENCE, denominator comes from LOCK. AST-003 bans literal integrity fields and AST-004 flags fail-open patterns. SCH-004 computed_by provenance. Corpus: LEARNED-BANK summarize.py, V6 audit_results.py:97.

mfl gatediff auto-generates GATE_DIFF.json. A loosen, or a clarify after failure, needs other-agent sign-off plus a new negative test; both versions are kept; post-edit results do not count until signed. Gates in protected rule sets go through governance. PAD-003 catches check claims that precede their artifacts.

ADMISSION.json is required before any roster above 2 CPU-h or 10,000 records. It covers the E0 analytic SNR and measured contrast, leave-one-out prompt ID, birth partitions, E1 acquisition preflight, and an oracle-upstream chain smoke. Cycle 0 may stop but never tune. Positive transfer: the native_next INPUT_STATE_NOT_ADMITTED pattern.

Teaching-port trio for each channel and sign; frame-type digests equal between calibration and query; resume round-trip on checkpoints; fixture-parameter diff against SPEC; CHECK_MANIFEST with DROPPED reasons; per-world birth gates in the runner. Corpus: v4 negated sign, [-0:] replay slice, cursor-less checkpoint.

mfl preflight (AST-010 module collisions, PRE-001 JSON round-trip, numpy scalars, identity-field equality, boundary slices, vendor byte-diff). runtime_guard RTG-001/002 isolated mode and closure. Every new defect appends to INCIDENTS, and closure requires a fixture.

Write-before-assert (AST-008, RES-001). ResourceLedger in every runner records all attempts, including tuning, surrogate, failed, countermodel and audit runs. Two-source count reconciliation (RES-002). Deterministic native event counters are primary. Lineage-wide compute in claims. Instruments validated on known values in self-tests.

Profile one complete history; analytic dose reachability; atomic paired units; preregistered contingency rules; post-lock cap changes need a DECISION with ops-only scope; RESOURCE_STOP_VERDICT_ON_COMPLETED_UNITS is mandatory. Caps are enforced in runtime_guard from AUTHORIZATION.

loopkit/stats.py is the only decision module (STA-001..007): OC simulation, Hoeffding or UNRESOLVED for zero variance, intersection-union, a 2SE rule for DEV winners with shrinkage noted, PILOT label for fewer than 8 worlds with MDE and worst world, ALPHA_LEDGER for the program-level error budget.

Closed-enum CLAIM.json and claimlint CLM-001..009: banned soft words near gates, 'confirm' only on sealed worlds, native/core only with demonstrated lineage, 'approved' only with a DECISION reference, held numbers at the prespecified checkpoint, number-artifact binding, enum evidence levels. Corpus: CLS 'largely met', 'Native confirmation' on D2.

SPEC.LINEAGE with ops retained/adapted/replaced and inheritance_status defaulting to not_demonstrated; native whitelist, with anything outside labelled hybrid. Answer-path provenance per scored byte. record_type enum (USER_ADOPTED, SCIENTIFIC, ENGINEERING_REFERENCE, CANDIDATE). Op-signature index LED-008: renamed recipes inherit negatives.

Append-only ledgers with narrowed_by and superseded_by; CURRENT_*, catalog and memo views generated (LED-004); narrowed-fact caveat check (LED-006); staleness check at session-start (LED-005); design directories hash-frozen; hypothesis lifecycle with transfer or retirement on substrate change. Corpus: P036 uncaveated, stale CURRENT_ARITHMETIC.

mfl lint citations (CIT-001/002) checks quoted value, comparator, decoder and substrate tags and caveats against UNIT_FACTS with metric definitions. CLM-007 bans mixing provenance. Reviewer must trace at least one number to code. Corpus: 7/8 vs 6/8, 99.22% from a different decoder, tally without its caveat.

FAILURE_CLASSES trigger predicates make applicable checks mandatory (LED-009). Block 6 PREDICTIONS hashed into the lock. PREDICTION_SCORES at publish with transfer annotations. Incident closure requires an executable check plus fixtures. R-levels; recurrence after close reopens the class (MM-7). KB backtests.

REV-001..006: identity from trailers and JSON (not git author names), cross-agent at T2 and cross-family at T3, executed checks with committed scripts, UNVERIFIED label for read-only findings, status-enum reconciliation, identical-review detection. Review canaries measure reviewer recall. Owner spot-checks anchor both agents.

AUTHORIZATION schema with verbatim text, options shown, separate recommendation, stage booleans, caps and conditionals evaluated by another identity (AUTH-001..007). Default small caps for silent grants. Constraint-touching proposals flagged REQUIRES_USER_DECISION and blocked for the same iteration. runtime_guard enforces caps. Corpus: '(Recommended)', self-judged 'If yes', grant growth.

LNK-001/002 link checks (no /Users, /home or /tmp paths; relative targets exist). Session-start MFL-002 requires the KB on the branch and the canonical head as ancestor. A minimal verification subset is published. UNVERIFIABLE_IN_REPO facts are capped at R1. Review scripts are committed repo-relative. Branch from the canonical head.

minifly-loop-governance: protected paths with MANIFEST self-hash; computed strictness classification (removal or unclassifiable = loosen); owner DECISION for loosenings; corpus 100%, canary recall and the false-positive budget required to merge; conflict-of-interest rule; prospective loop_version in every lock; tripwires TRP-001..003; history re-validation against hook bypass; meta-progress only MM-1; structure meters paired with distinguishability gates; lessons reconciled by the other agent; canary-literal fixes rejected.

designs.ceremony_cost:
Cost scales with stake, and the tier is computed rather than chosen.

T0 (saved-data reanalysis, memo, no learner execution, no pointer change). Artifacts: CLAIM.json only if numbers are published. Checks: mfl lint claim, text and links, under 5 s. No review is required; it is labelled self. Overhead is minutes.

T1 (DEV-only bounded run, <= 2 CPU-h and <= 10,000 records, output stamped DEV_NOT_EVIDENCE). Artifacts: SPEC-lite (contract fields, LINEAGE, objective distance), AUTHORIZATION, a CYCLE_PLAN and CYCLE_RECORD per cycle, runtime ledgers written automatically by runtime_guard, and a capped CLAIM. Cycle-0 checks run only where a trigger fires; for example, testbed validity is needed only if the task is new, and the E0 contrast only if the front end, init or read path changed. Labelled self-review is allowed. Gates take under 10 s. The target is 30 minutes or less of agent time per delivery.

T2 (cited pilot or official run, any E2+ attempt, or anything above T1 caps). Artifacts: full SPEC, PREDICTIONS and U2C files; ADMISSION, MUTATION_SCORE, CONTROL_DIFFERENTIAL and REDUCER_FIXTURES; LOCK pushed before scoring; a clean-room reducer by the other agent; two cross-agent reviews per delivery (design and post-run), not one per cycle; CLAIM, PREDICTION_SCORES and FACT_DELTAS. Safeguard compute (cycle 0, mutants, countermodels, review reruns) is capped at max(10% of roster compute, 1 CPU-h). Exceeding the cap is a signal to simplify the testbed, not to skip checks.

T3 (sealed confirmation, adoption, CURRENT pointer change, E3 promotion). Everything in T2, plus evaluator-salted commit-reveal seeds, a zero-touch holdout check, an ALPHA_LEDGER row, a verbatim owner grant, a cross-family fresh-context reviewer and an owner decision for adoption. This adds about one calendar day of review latency.

Anti-padding rules.
- Content lives in JSON fields produced by tools; prose is short and rendered.
- No per-cycle audit essays, no 'no parameter changed' disclaimers (81 of 168 cycle notes had them), no compliance prose.
- PAD-001 flags byte-identical files; PAD-002 flags boilerplate repeated across 3 or more deliveries.
- A review counts only if it contains executed outputs.
- Checks apply through trigger predicates, so not every check runs every time.
- New rules start advisory, so friction is measured before enforcement.
- MM-9 tracks safeguard CPU share, agent turns, artifacts and owner decisions per tier.
- The sunset path lets the owner demote checks with zero catches over 10 or more deliveries.
- Owner decisions are batched at the census, except launch grants.

Why the cost pays back. Predictable or void zeros in the history: V6-R1 ran 34,816 records at 0%, decidable from its own design formulas; NATIVE-BIND V2.1 spent 147,456 records with taught OLD at 0-8.3%; Package B spent about 80 core-hours on a void E3; STOP-ONLY spent 225,792 records against a weak comparator. The admission check that native_next adopted saved a 43,520-record roster for seconds of computation. The T2 safeguard budget is small next to any one of these.
designs.rollout:
Phase 0 (this delivery). No experiments; read-only on history; nothing frozen is altered.
(a) Add the 13 skills under .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, each under 400 lines, with references/: SPEC_V1.md, MUTANT_ZOO.md, STRATA_AND_WITNESSES.md, BANNED_PHRASES.md, PROTECTED_PATHS.md, CANARY_PROTOCOL.md, BACKTEST_PROTOCOL.md.
(b) Add loopkit/, stdlib-only, run with python3 -I. Its self-tests and corpus run in under 30 s.
(c) Seed PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/LOOP/:
- FAILURE_CLASSES.json for FM-01..FM-30, with triggers, checks and incidents from the digest.
- UNIT_FACTS.jsonl for UF-01..UF-29 with statuses: UF-15 narrowed; UF-02 unverifiable_in_repo; UF-25 dev-only; UF-21 invalid axis.
- INCIDENTS.jsonl from the digest instances.
- HOLDOUT_REGISTRY.jsonl, marking known reused worlds and items burned or dev: 202610143901-03, the value-retention held orbits, the LEARNED-BANK D1-D3 worlds and their 55-orbit universe.
- RULES.json with defaults, all advisory except governance and protected invariants.
- PROTECTED_INVARIANTS.json and CONSTRAINTS.json as DRAFT_AWAITING_OWNER, with objective_targets=TARGET_UNSET.
- regression_corpus with dirty and clean fixtures for FM-01..FM-30.
- RETRO_EXPECTED.json listing the 17 spot-checked incidents.
- Tripwires.
(d) Add a root AGENTS.md pointer of about 15 lines: read .claude/skills/minifly-loop/SKILL.md first; run mfl session-start and mfl gate; protected paths; trailers; the owner owns constraints. Also add the .githooks/ scripts and a .claude/settings.json hook config, both inactive until the owner enables them (git config core.hooksPath .githooks).
(e) Run mfl selftest --mutate-tools, mfl corpus run and mfl retro --all (static), and publish RETRO_FINDINGS as a T0 claim labelled NO_VERDICT_CHANGE.
(f) Mr. Zhou reviews and signs CONSTRAINTS, PROTECTED_INVARIANTS and loop v1.0.0 through a DECISIONS row, and optionally sets objective targets.

Phase 1 (first prospective use).
(a) Before anyone cites the in-flight LEARNED-BANK verdict, run mfl retro and an independent review of it. Known findings: summarize.py fails open on missing arms and worlds; the lock omits imported modules; T-PAR's distance from E3; the post-data amendment. These are appended as REVIEW and INCIDENTS rows, and the verdict itself is not altered.
(b) Apply schema v1 to the next native design at T2 with Codex executing and Claude evaluating and reviewing, or the reverse.
(c) Rules stay advisory for 2 deliveries, except governance and protected invariants. Measure MM-9 ceremony cost and false positives.

Phase 2 (first held-out evaluation of the loop).
(a) First canary batch: 10 items with at least 3 clean, authored by the owner or by a fresh session that did not write loopkit.
(b) First KB backtest at T=2026-10-15 over the 10-15..10-23 deliveries, with base-rate, contract-only and KB forecasters.
(c) First LOOP_HEALTH.json and owner digest.

Phase 3 (enforcement and cadence). Rules flip to enforced if their false-positive budget held. The owner chooses a git-level anchor: CODEOWNERS with branch protection, or signed loop tags. Meta-eval runs at every census or every 5 deliveries. Burned canaries go into the corpus, and sunset reviews are batched to the owner.

Migration. Schema changes follow semver through governance. Historical deliveries remain readable via retro mode and are never rewritten.
risks: Meta-Goodhart is mitigated, not eliminated. Every agent has write access, so protections are tamper-evident (hashes, history re-validation, tripwires) rather than tamper-proof, until the owner enables CODEOWNERS with branch protection or signed tags.

Checks may overfit the historical corpus, the way a lookup table memorizes taught items. Sealed canaries counter this, but batches are small (about 10), so recall estimates are noisy. Treat them as alarms, not scores.

False positives may block legitimate exploration or drive work into T0/T1 salami-slicing. Mitigations: computed tiers using cumulative lineage compute, an advisory period, a false-positive budget, waivers, and a cheap T1 path. Residual friction will remain and must be measured (MM-9).
A one-way tightening ratchet can still produce ceremony creep despite trigger-scoped checks. The sunset path depends on the owner actually reviewing demotions at census.
Codex and Claude may share blind spots or effectively collude. Review canaries and owner spot-checks are the only anchors outside both, and they depend on owner time.
Prediction registration can become rote, for example by copying the base rate. Proper scoring shows zero skill, but the effort is still spent. Keep predictions to primary and guard endpoints only.

KB backtests can leak: fresh sessions may infer outcomes from naming (r2, revised) or from memo phrasing. With few post-T deliveries, confidence intervals will be wide. Label results accordingly and do not over-interpret them.

MM-1 may stay at 'none' for a long time, given a native E3 base rate near 0 of 8. That creates pressure to relax gates or reframe component wins as progress. The only legitimate route is an owner DECISION, and the component-bridge rule keeps such claims scored.
The static AST closure can miss dynamic loading, data-file code or vendored stores. The runtime closure assertion and fail-closed handling of dynamic imports cover most cases, not all.

The U2C determinacy witness and the leave-units-out test add evaluator complexity and paired-world cost. A wrong witness can wrongly exclude or include strata, so the witness choice is itself a reviewed SPEC field.
Retro findings could be misread as re-adjudicating history or as grounds to alter frozen verdicts. Outputs are labelled RETRO_FINDINGS_NO_VERDICT_CHANGE and never written into delivery directories.
Owner attention is a bottleneck: decisions are required for loosenings, T3 actions, constraint touches and targets. Batching at census helps but could slow urgent legitimate work.
Schema v1 lock-in: early schema mistakes propagate. Semver migrations through governance add their own overhead.
The countermodel ladder is finite, and a novel shortcut may pass. The reviewer's cheapest-shortcut credit and governed additions to the ladder are the remedy, after the fact.
The objective lacks numeric targets (TARGET_UNSET). Until the owner sets them, per-sample and per-compute efficiency can only be reported as a frontier, not gated.

fatal_flaws: None is fatal, but several issues need fixing before freeze. Check ADM-CTRL-DIGEST passes whenever the lesion arm's state digest differs from W's. Any nondeterminism (RNG draw order, timestamps in state) makes the digests differ even when the lesion was never delivered. writes_by_channel is counted by the executor's runner, and in Package B the writes were made by the same branch_allows policy the counter would likely reuse. The fix: count writes at the write site, and require the lesioned channel's digest to equal its birth or passive digest.

The tier is max(declared, computed from lock.budget). lock.budget is itself declared by the agent, and nothing accumulates cost across a lineage. Splitting one study into several tier-1 deliveries therefore avoids the tier-2 review and canary.

ENDPOINT_LOCK.json has about 30 required top-level blocks, closure_sha256 among them, and the design names no scaffold or 'lock init/build' command. Under time pressure agents will hand-copy the previous lock and edit it. The '20-30 minute' cost estimate is optimistic for the first few deliveries.

LOCK-06 requires the lock commit to precede the results commit. Codex's actual practice is local development followed by one 'Publish X results' commit (43d04b5e, 3065bb1a, 43b07e89). Local tier-1 ordering is trivially forgeable, and tier-2 needs a push or attestation the owner often has not authorized mid-delivery.
Every protected-path change needs an owner UD, including pure tightenings. The incident -> check loop therefore stalls on owner bandwidth.

CLM-15 requires OUTPUTS.jsonl publication at tier 2. That conflicts with the established 'publish without raw data' policy and with bundle sizes (STOP-ONLY is 949M). The scorer must read zip or gz bundles, and the policy needs an owner decision.
best_ideas: A canonical program-wide scorer plus shortcut ladder: a delivery supplies only decide(rows, lock). This removes the per-delivery common-mode auditor at its root.

LAD-02 substitution test: substitute the best shortcut's rows for the candidate's; if the locked rule still PASSES, the gate fails as non-discriminating. Cheap, mechanical, and it catches STOP-ONLY vs FIXED_1 directly.
Exactly four choke points (lock, roster, official, publish/pointer), mapped onto the user's loop. Easy to remember and to obey under time pressure.
RED-01..09 synthetic fixtures run against the decision rule before any data exist. They catch the LEARNED-BANK fail-open summarize.py class.
Generated CLAIM.json headline; pointers are v1 copies of CLAIM fields; no bare pass booleans.
An explicit, justified 'deliberately left out' list, which counters ceremony creep.
Phase 0 retro on real history, with a measured false-flag rate on deliveries believed clean, before the owner freezes v1. No agent behaviour changes until then.

ENDPOINT_LOCK replaces the prose design block rather than adding to it, and AUTHORIZATION.json extends existing practice. Good fit with the SOURCE_LOCK, AUTHORIZATION and SPEC files already in the repo.
Gate cost is measured: CLAIM.ceremony_minutes, gate runtimes, and a prune review of checks with zero catches.
GOV-SEP: a checker or skill change can never share a commit range with a delivery.
Reviewer-seeded canary on the delivery's own artifacts at tier 2; held-out incident recall as the checker's score.

fatal_flaws: Two agents cannot staff five roles. T2 starts at more than 1 CPU-h, more than 5k records, or any result entering the ledger as a fact, which covers almost every delivery in the catalog (V6-R1 34,816 records; LEARNED-BANK about 11 CPU-h). At T2 an evaluator-owner from the other principal must push EVAL_PLAN, gates, reducer and SEAL_COMMIT before the executor's first implementation commit. Claude sessions are ephemeral and Codex runs locally on the owner's machine, so in-flight Codex work blocks waiting for a Claude session.

PROTECTED_MANIFEST self-verification runs on every rigor.py call, so any drift returns exit 3 on every subcommand until an SCP plus a governor code lands. Drift includes a skill typo fix or a repo-wide line-ending normalization of the kind already done in 6c4dfe4c. One mistake bricks the whole kit, which invites agents to bypass it.

Governor one-time codes: Mr. Zhou must run a TTY-only command in his own terminal and type codes for every T2 launch, and twice at T3. Seal salts must be escrowed outside the repo, and ephemeral sessions lose them, giving UNINFORMATIVE_SEAL_BROKEN. That is high owner burden with no evidence he will accept it.

instrument.py adds sys.addaudithook OPEN_LOG heartbeats, input taps, RUNTIME_CLOSURE and a resource ledger inside every runner. That requires refactoring every learner family before the kit gives any value.

Ten skills plus 15 modules, blind/full handoff packs with ACK cross-witnessing, committed SESSION_PROMPTS, and typed CYCLE_PLAN/CYCLE_RECORD with revision taxonomies. The typed cycle files are exactly the per-cycle files that the history shows turn into identical boilerplate.
Shingle-Jaccard COMMON_MODE_SUSPECT will false-positive on legitimately similar numpy or reducer code written independently by two LLMs.
best_ideas: Tier from cumulative lineage cost across same-protocol siblings, which defeats salami-slicing.
Single-agent degraded mode with REVIEW_DEBT rows that must be repaid before adoption or pointer changes. This fits the reality that the other agent is often unavailable.
Hand-offs carry only '<commit sha> <path>' plus a request; relayed reviews are stored verbatim with a sha256. Cheap and robust.
reconcile legacy-map: converts the V51 AUDIT.json statuses into a closed enum. Directly reuses existing practice.
Findings without an executed check are UNVERIFIED and carry no weight. A zero-finding review must still list its executed attempts.
Cheapest-shortcut bounty for the reviewer.
Default caps for terse grants (at most 2 CPU-h, at most 5k records, dev only). Grants with conditions are written as predicates, which someone other than the beneficiary evaluates.
Evaluator writes the reducer from SPEC text only. Worth keeping as a T3/confirmation-only requirement.
Composition map with unit-ablation difference-in-differences as the E3 causal control.
Ceremony time logged under 'governance', with a per-tier budget share.

fatal_flaws: Every ledger is a hash-chained JSONL (prev_hash), including DECISIONS, SKILL_CHANGES and CANARY_COMMITMENTS. Codex works on codex/minifly-consolidated-20261023 and Claude on claude/* branches, so two branches appending to the same ledger are guaranteed to break the chain on merge. A broken chain in those ledgers is GOVERNANCE_BREACH (exit 3), which blocks every stage. Plain append-only JSONL with a union merge driver is needed instead.

Enforcement relies on mechanisms that do not reach Codex or are off by default. A Claude PreToolUse hook never runs for Codex; .githooks is inactive until the owner sets core.hooksPath; and session-start re-validates every commit since a marker. Under time pressure agents skip a slow, fragile session-start.

runtime_guard requires the learner to run as a separate OS process exchanging bytes only, plus an input tap, audit hooks and caps enforcement inside every runner. That is a full runner rewrite per learner family before any delivery can reach T2.

At T2 a delivery must produce SPEC, PREDICTIONS, CHECK_MANIFEST, the six U2C files, the ADMISSION suite (five files), LOCK, CYCLE plans and records, reviews, PREMORTEM, CLAIM, PREDICTION_SCORES and FACT_DELTAS. T2 covers any E2+ attempt or cited pilot, so the heavy path is the common path. Thirteen skills is too many to load reliably.

Merge requirement: 100% detect and 100% clean-pass over dirty and clean mini-deliveries for all of FM-01..FM-30, plus --mutate-tools, before any governance change. That is a large up-front corpus build before the first prospective delivery gets value.
'Each cycle catches at least one seeded bug' and per-reviewer PREMORTEM probabilities are recurring rituals of the padding kind the history warns about.
best_ideas: U2C made concrete. Strata S0-S4, with S0 trivial (zero or identity operand) and S1 presentation twins excluded from E3 headlines. An evaluator-side determinacy witness (pair_rectangle). A unit-dependency index from leave-units-out paired worlds. This is the clearest operationalization of 'generalize from unit learned knowledge'.
R0-R4 transfer levels for both facts and checks. Only R3+ (held-out canary, or a later prediction that beats the base rate) is 'transferable'. A research-level E-ladder.
New or tightened rules run advisory for 2 deliveries before enforcement. This is the single most adoption-friendly mechanism in any of the three designs.
loop_version is recorded in every LOCK, and a delivery is gated under its recorded version. This gives prospective application and lets in-flight work finish under old rules.
Failure-class trigger predicates over SPEC fields, so checks run only when relevant. Ceremony scales with what changed, not with a fixed checklist.
