implementation_work_packages.title: Governance, selftest, held-out canaries and read-only retro (governance.py, retro.py)
implementation_work_packages.instructions:
Source of truth: the MRK-1 spec, sections 7.4 (GOV-*, HELD-*), 7.7 (selftest), 12.3 (held-out protocol), 12.4 (retro acceptance) and 13 (change classes, direction map, process). Python 3.9 or later, stdlib only.

(1) cmd_selftest
- For each fixture dir in tools/minifly_check/corpus (excluding _build and heldout), run every command listed in EXPECTED.json in-process with --repo-root <fixture>/repo and TimelineGit(<fixture>).
- Collect the fired ids (FAIL or MISSING) and the WARN ids, then assert must_fire, must_not_fire, must_warn, expected_exit and the 'expect' JSON-pointer assertions against the produced files.
- Run canary on C00a with seed 'c0ffee'.
- --mutate replaces each CHECKS entry in turn with always-PASS and always-FAIL stubs. Report 'not exercised' and 'no clean coverage' per id.
- On success, write the cache file used by SELF-01.
- Runtime target is under 20 s without --mutate.

(2) cmd_governance --base B --head H
- Compute changed protected paths via ctx.git.changed_paths and PROTECTED.json.
- Classify every change with the table and direction map of section 13.2:
  - RULES and EXPECTED diffs by id;
  - CONSTRAINTS by key and direction;
  - SKILL.md by removed lines containing minifly_check, MUST, NEVER, must or never;
  - code edits by running the head checker and the base checker (extracted with 'git archive B tools/minifly_check' into a tempdir and run as a subprocess with python3 -I) on base and head corpora, then comparing fired sets.
- Unclassifiable changes are loosen.
- Implement GOV-SELF, GOV-SEP, GOV-CLASS, GOV-REV (review record in PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/KB/GOVERNANCE/REVIEW_<id>.json by the other family, cited in a Governance-Review trailer), GOV-UD, GOV-NUM (every changed number in the verbatim text), GOV-MONO, GOV-APPEND, GOV-SKILL (frontmatter parse, description of 1024 characters or fewer, body under 400 lines, AGENTS.md lists all five skills) and GOV-COI (used by the official and publish bundles).

(3) cmd_heldout
- seal: HMAC-SHA256 counter-mode keystream XOR of a tar-like concatenation (a json manifest plus files) into corpus/heldout/sealed/<B>.bin, and a printed CANARY_COMMITMENTS row.
- reveal: verify the hashes and decrypt into a tempdir.
- score: run the checker at --checker-sha via git archive on the revealed fixtures and write a HELDOUT report to the --out path.
- Implement HELD-01..03.

(4) retro.py
- cmd_retro (--all | <dir>) --out DIR. Refuse an --out inside any delivery dir. Never import or execute historical code. Read files directly, and use 'git show <ref>:<path>' for branches such as origin/charming-head.
- Emit RETRO_ANNOTATION rows {checker_sha256, delivery, check_id, status PASS|FLAG|NOT_APPLICABLE, reason, evidence_paths}.
- Adapters: R-LOCKTIME, R-CLOSURE, R-LITERAL, R-FAILOPEN, R-CLAIM, R-POINTER, R-CTRL (gzip receipts under minifly_b/results/science), R-CATALOG, R-AUTH, R-PATHS and R-INERT (identical arm summaries).
- Treat a commit adding 3 or more delivery dirs as NOT_APPLICABLE_BULK_IMPORT for timing.
- Print acceptance statistics against the section 12.4 FLAG and quiet lists, embedded as a constant.
- Retro exits nonzero only on its own crash.

(5) Tests
- Classification: threshold loosen, check added, EXPECTED id removed, skill NEVER line removed.
- GOV-NUM with and without the number in the verbatim text.
- GOV-SEP with a mixed range.
- Heldout seal and reveal round-trip, plus a tampered bundle.
- Retro on a synthetic legacy dir: literal integrity flagged, summarize-style 'is not False' flagged.
- --out inside a delivery refused.

Acceptance: unit tests pass. Running the full selftest green is the integration acceptance after WP2-WP5 and WP7 land; report any mismatch to the owning work package instead of editing its files.

implementation_work_packages.title: Regression corpus and EXPECTED.json (generator plus committed fixtures)
implementation_work_packages.instructions:
Source of truth: the MRK-1 spec, sections 12.2 (fixture table), 7.3 (TimelineGit fixture format), 7.7 (EXPECTED semantics) and 8 (schemas; also read tools/minifly_check/SCHEMAS.md once WP1 lands). For author independence, do not read tools/minifly_check/*.py implementation code: write fixtures only from the spec and SCHEMAS.md.

(1) corpus/_build/base/
- Hand-build a clean miniature v1 repo:
  - one delivery dir (for example minifly_corpus_base_dev_v1_20261101);
  - ENDPOINT_LOCK.json at E3 target, addition_single_digit task, pair_rectangle witness;
  - arms W (candidate), NPT (no_prior_teaching), SHUF, FROZEN, ORACLE (oracle_plumbing), plus CEILING_A, CEILING_B, FLOOR_* per the CONSTRAINTS grid;
  - 8 official MAIN worlds, 2 dev worlds, 1 rehearsal world, 1 technical world, about 10 items per pool;
  - SOURCE_LOCK.json, params.json, AUTHORIZATION.json, ADMISSION.json, receipts with per-channel digests (birth, post_first, end), TAUGHT manifests per arm, FIXTURES.jsonl, admission, dev, rehearsal and official OUTPUTS with stream_hex;
  - runlog/ATTEMPTS.jsonl, runlog/CYCLES.jsonl, review/REVIEW.json with executed-check files;
  - a PROJECT_DOCUMENTS/KB overlay: CONSTRAINTS.json (draft values of section 13.1) and minimal ledgers.
- Native and runner .py files are tiny stubs, parsed but never executed.
- Compute by hand, and document in corpus/_build/base/EXPECTED_VALUES.md: the strata, determinacy, ladder best shortcut, G and verdict.

(2) corpus/_build/build_corpus.py
- A stdlib script that deterministically produces every fixture dir in the section 12.2 table (C00a-C00f, C01-C30 with suffixes, G01-G05, K01) by copying the base and applying named mutation functions.
- Each fixture dir gets FIXTURE.json {id, title, fm_ids, source_incident, kind dirty|clean}, repo/, timeline.json and history/.
- Commit both the script and its output. selftest never runs the builder.
- Fixtures must be small (each under about 200 KB).

(3) EXPECTED.json
- One entry per fixture: commands (for example ['gate','--stage','roster','<delivery>'], ['score','<delivery>','--role','official']), must_fire, must_not_fire, must_warn, expected_exit per command, expect (JSON-pointer to value, for example '/verdict': 'FAIL', '/headline' substring checks expressed as {'contains': 'FIXED_1'}), source_incident and fm_ids.
- Use exactly the check ids of the spec. Clean fixtures expect exit 0 everywhere and nothing fired.

(4) corpus/README.md
- How to add a fixture from an incident (through governance only).

(5) corpus/heldout/README.md
- The sealed batch protocol of section 12.3. No held-out fixtures are created now.

Acceptance:
- Every FM-01..FM-30 has at least one fixture.
- build_corpus.py regenerates byte-identical output.
- JSON files parse.
- Each dirty fixture differs from base only by its documented mutation (state this in FIXTURE.json 'mutation').

implementation_work_packages.title: Skills A: minifly-research-loop and minifly-e3-design (with references)
implementation_work_packages.instructions:
Source of truth: the MRK-1 spec, sections 6.1 and 6.2 (frontmatter descriptions verbatim, section outlines, key rules), 3 (stage map, typed cycles, FAIL table, forbidden moves, not-required list), 4 (tiers) and 9 (measurement).

Format and style
- Each SKILL.md starts with YAML frontmatter: name (exactly minifly-research-loop and minifly-e3-design) and description, copied verbatim from the spec and kept at 1024 characters or fewer.
- Bodies stay under 400 lines.
- Write for any agent (Codex or Claude). Use no tool-specific instructions, only shell commands of the form 'python3 -I tools/minifly_check/minifly_check.py ...' (abbreviate as MFC after defining it).
- Open each body with an 'If you only read this' box of at most 5 lines.
- Link to tools/minifly_check/SCHEMAS.md for field-level schemas instead of duplicating them.
- Avoid ceremony: no templates that invite padding, no compliance boilerplate.
- Use imperative rules with concrete historical examples cited by repo path: Package B minifly_b/REPORT.md:12-26; STOP-ONLY minifly_address_capacity_v1_dev_20261023/REPORT.md:7; V6-R1 minifly_v6_r1_dev_20261023/REVISION.md:40-52; LEARNED-BANK origin/charming-head minifly_learned_bank_v1_20261024/cycles/CYCLE2.md.

minifly-research-loop
- Implement the 10 sections of spec 6.1.
- STAGES.md: a per-stage checklist with the artifacts read and written and the exact commands, mirroring spec 3.1 and 3.2.
- AUTHORIZATION.md: how to record a grant (verbatim, options_shown, separate recommendation, stage booleans, caps restated in the owner's words or the defaults, predicate grammar {artifact, pointer, op, value}, examples of neutral option framing, pressure-phrase handling, REQUIRES_USER_DECISION).

minifly-e3-design
- Implement the 12 sections of spec 6.2.
- RULE_GRAMMAR.md: the declarative primary, gates and guards grammar with field meanings, an E1 example, an E3 example and an E3 promotion example with udi; how comparators, ladder subsets and aggregators work; and why no delivery decision code is allowed.
- ADMISSION_AND_RUNNER_CONTRACT.md: what the runner must emit (OUTPUTS with stream_hex up to gen_cap ignoring EOS, TAUGHT per arm, receipts with per-channel digests at birth, post_first and end, write counters at the mutation site, replay flags, write-before-assert), what admit.py emits (CEILING_*/FLOOR_* rows, FIXTURES.jsonl, ADMISSION.json with structure meters), and that every counted run goes through 'launch'.
- STRATA_WITNESS_UDI.md: S0-S4 definitions with worked single-digit and multi-digit addition examples, the pair_rectangle and column_closure witnesses with a worked example, the UDI variant construction and the G computation example.

Acceptance
- Frontmatter parses as YAML.
- Descriptions are byte-identical to the spec.
- Bodies are under 400 lines.
- Every command and check id mentioned exists in spec section 7.
- No contradictions with the spec.
